PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
3. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
4. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
5. **Can it be one line?** One line.
6. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project. Two rungs work → take the
higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the right one.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment (`// ponytail: this exists`), simple reads as intent, not ignorance. Shortcut with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic)? The comment names the ceiling and the upgrade path: `# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`.

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Anton L\.claude\skills\design # Design The front door for all design work. Read this before writing a line of UI. **The rule this skill exists to enforce:** > **Brand derives direction. Skills supply craft. Themes are the last resort.** Every previous failure in this codebase came from inverting that: a specialist skill set the direction and the brand got repainted in the skill author's palette. Direction comes from the subject's own evidence. Skills contribute spacing, states, motion, and mechanics *inside* that direction. This file dispatches. It does not teach — the references carry the full detail and are the source of truth. Load the ones your branch names; never load a catalogue to make one pick. Over-eager loading is the largest avoidable cost of running this skill. --- ## Disciplines that hold across every branch Not branch-specific. They apply to new work, audit, redesign, study, and component-scope alike. **Read [`chain-discipline.md`](references/chain-discipline.md) first — it is resident, not routed.** It is the one file in this shelf that is about the chain rather than the page: nine rules won from a five-day run that spent 37 build rounds on 10 orders and still missed the level. Every rule in it came from a measurement, a review or a plan that lied to this chain and was believed. They govern how you measure (M1–M3), how you verify (V1–V2), how you orchestrate (O1–O2) and how you review (R1–R2), and the round ladder in § 5 is why the spiral happened. No builder, reviewer or orchestrator runs without it. 1. **Pre-emit self-critique.** Before handing back any output, score it 1–5 on six axes — Philosophy, Hierarchy, Execution, Specificity, Restraint, Variety. Anything **< 3** triggers a revision pass. Stamp the six scores at the top of the artifact (`/* design · pre-emit critique: P5 H4 E5 S4 R5 V5 */`). See [`slop-test.md`](references/slop-test.md) § Pre-emit self-critique. 2. **Honest copy — no fabricated content.** If the user did not supply a metric, do not invent one. Stat-led layouts, comparison rows, and proof bars must use real numbers, a placeholder (`—` plus a labelled grey block, "metric to confirm"), or a different macrostructure. *"+47 % conversion"*, *"trusted by 50,000+ teams"*, and *"10× faster"* are slop the moment they're invented. Same rule for testimonials, logos, and case-study counts. See [`anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md) § Invented metrics and gate **46**. 3. **Locked tokens — no mid-render improvisation.** Once the direction is settled, every colour and every `font-family` declaration must reference a named token (`var(--color-accent)`, `font-family: var(--font-display)`). Inline OKLCH / hex / `rgb()` values, or a `font-family: "Some Font"` that bypasses the token block, are not allowed. If a value is needed that doesn't exist as a token, lift it into the token block as a new named variable, then reference it. See [`anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md) § Mid-render token improvisation and gate **48**. 4. **Re-drawn chrome forbidden.** Never hand-build fake browser bars (URL pill + traffic-light dots), fake phone frames, fake code-block windows (mock title bar + dots wrapping a `
`), or fake IDE chrome — the user's environment already supplies real chrome. Use real screenshots wrapped in a `

# V3g · godkända effekter (skyddade)

Varje effekt nedan har Anton bedömt som bra. En runda får inte ändra dem om briefen inte
uttryckligen säger det, och ingen av dem får bli sämre mätt med `section_probe.py`.
Baslinjen är `shots/section-probe-baseline.json`. Den skrivs när loopfixen är gjord, eftersom
dagens siffror bär loopens kostnad.

| Effekt | Var | Vad som är bra (Antons ord) | Signatur att hålla |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tesrubriken reser sig och står | `#tes`, `.tes-top` pin 0,9 vh + char-rise | "Det första intrycket är digitalt … var bättre" i V3f | p95 i `#tes` ≤ V3f-nivå (33 ms) utan loop; rubriken helt synlig ≥ 40 vh |
| Rubrikerna i allmänhet | alla `headline-40/50` | "rubrikerna blev mycket bättre" (V3f) | står stilla och hela ≥ 40 vh (motion.md läsregel) |
| Kontakten, kortet lämnas över | `#kontakt` | "även kontaktsidan" (V3f) | kortet vänder sig självt vid 0,7; heron speglad |
| Showcase-mekanismen | `#showcase` | "showcasen är bättre", "behåll mekanismen" (V3g R2) | en pin skapad en gång; övertoning mellan steg; räknare + mintspår |
| Övertoning vid casebyte | `activateCase` | ingen hård övergång (V3g R1–R2) | inget scrollY-hopp > baslinjen vid klick |

Underkänt, får inte återkomma: stegrubrik i displayskala och jättesiffra i rutan (F-019);
numerisk scrub och Lenis-standardtempo (F-020); refresh-loop via iframe-omladdning (F-021).

1	# V3g · showcasen blir mjuk · spec R1
2	
3	V3g är en kopia av V3f. **Bara `#exempelcase` → `#showcase` rörs.** Komposition, färg, copy och
4	alla andra sektioner är orörda. V3f står kvar som arm A.
5	
6	Antons dom 2026-09-24: rubrikerna och kontakten blev bättre. Men klicket ger en hård övergång,
7	besökaren låses in i ett hackigt scroll-fängelse där exempelsidan hoppar, och listan bredvid
8	är statisk trots att markeringen byts. Han vill att allt blir mjukare och att det provas med en
9	**ruta med text bredvid som byts ut och tonar över till nästa**, som i V3d men i V3f:s stil.
10	
11	## Grundorsaker i V3f (rättas alla)
12	
13	| # | Orsak | Var | Rättning |
14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| 1 | `activateCase` dödar och återskapar pinnen synkront vid klicket, före `lenis.scrollTo` | `setupDesktopEngine`, r. ~1306–1360 | Pinnen skapas EN gång vid init och dödas aldrig |
16	| 2 | Hōrai-iframens `src` sätts först vid klick, vilket ger en navigation under övergången | `activateCase` | Båda iframes laddas vid `requestIdleCallback` efter `load` |
17	| 3 | Två utjämningslager: Lenis `lerp:0.1` + `scrub:0.6` | ScrollTrigger.create | `scrub:true`. Lenis är det enda lagret |
18	| 4 | `caseY` rör sig på 45 % av segmentet och står still 55 %, vilket ger ryck och stopp | r. 1265–1270 | Ny kurva, se B |
19	| 5 | Listan är ett dragspel som knäpper med klass vid heltalsgränser | `setRowState` + CSS `.row-body` | Textrutan i C, skrubbad övertoning |
20	| 6 | Pinlängden räknas om per case, så ett byte kräver `refresh` | `end: n × innerHeight` | Fast längd, se A |
21	
22	## A. Pinnen och entrén
23	
24	- **En** ScrollTrigger för `#showcase` skapas vid init (desktop ≥ 768, via `gsap.matchMedia`):
25	  `pin:'.showcase-stage'`, `scrub:true`, `start:'top top'`,
26	  `end: () => '+=' + Math.round(6 * 0.75 * window.innerHeight)`, `invalidateOnRefresh:true`.
27	  - Längden är densamma för båda casen: 6 segment à 75 vh. Calyx med 5 ankare fördelar sina
28	    segment över samma längd.
29	  - `onUpdate` läser ett **aktuellt case** `C` ur en variabel. Ett casebyte byter variabeln, och
30	    pinnen rörs aldrig.
31	- **Klick på ett case** (`activateCase`):
32	  1. `aria-pressed`, `inert` och panelernas synlighet sätts.
33	  2. Panelen och iframen tonas över: den gamla ut på 0,3 s, den nya in på 0,35 s,
34	     `power2.out`, interruptibelt (`overwrite:'auto'`). Ingen `display:none` förrän utgången
35	     är klar.
36	  3. `C` byts och `updateShowcase(C, st.progress)` körs.
37	  4. `lenis.scrollTo('#showcase', {duration:1.4, easing: t => 1 - Math.pow(2, -10*t)})`.

# V3g · showcasen blir mjuk · spec R1

V3g är en kopia av V3f. **Bara `#exempelcase` → `#showcase` rörs.** Komposition, färg, copy och
alla andra sektioner är orörda. V3f står kvar som arm A.

Antons dom 2026-09-24: rubrikerna och kontakten blev bättre. Men klicket ger en hård övergång,
besökaren låses in i ett hackigt scroll-fängelse där exempelsidan hoppar, och listan bredvid
är statisk trots att markeringen byts. Han vill att allt blir mjukare och att det provas med en
**ruta med text bredvid som byts ut och tonar över till nästa**, som i V3d men i V3f:s stil.

## Grundorsaker i V3f (rättas alla)

| # | Orsak | Var | Rättning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `activateCase` dödar och återskapar pinnen synkront vid klicket, före `lenis.scrollTo` | `setupDesktopEngine`, r. ~1306–1360 | Pinnen skapas EN gång vid init och dödas aldrig |
| 2 | Hōrai-iframens `src` sätts först vid klick, vilket ger en navigation under övergången | `activateCase` | Båda iframes laddas vid `requestIdleCallback` efter `load` |
| 3 | Två utjämningslager: Lenis `lerp:0.1` + `scrub:0.6` | ScrollTrigger.create | `scrub:true`. Lenis är det enda lagret |
| 4 | `caseY` rör sig på 45 % av segmentet och står still 55 %, vilket ger ryck och stopp | r. 1265–1270 | Ny kurva, se B |
| 5 | Listan är ett dragspel som knäpper med klass vid heltalsgränser | `setRowState` + CSS `.row-body` | Textrutan i C, skrubbad övertoning |
| 6 | Pinlängden räknas om per case, så ett byte kräver `refresh` | `end: n × innerHeight` | Fast längd, se A |

## A. Pinnen och entrén

- **En** ScrollTrigger för `#showcase` skapas vid init (desktop ≥ 768, via `gsap.matchMedia`):
  `pin:'.showcase-stage'`, `scrub:true`, `start:'top top'`,
  `end: () => '+=' + Math.round(6 * 0.75 * window.innerHeight)`, `invalidateOnRefresh:true`.
  - Längden är densamma för båda casen: 6 segment à 75 vh. Calyx med 5 ankare fördelar sina
    segment över samma längd.
  - `onUpdate` läser ett **aktuellt case** `C` ur en variabel. Ett casebyte byter variabeln, och
    pinnen rörs aldrig.
- **Klick på ett case** (`activateCase`):
  1. `aria-pressed`, `inert` och panelernas synlighet sätts.
  2. Panelen och iframen tonas över: den gamla ut på 0,3 s, den nya in på 0,35 s,
     `power2.out`, interruptibelt (`overwrite:'auto'`). Ingen `display:none` förrän utgången
     är klar.
  3. `C` byts och `updateShowcase(C, st.progress)` körs.
  4. `lenis.scrollTo('#showcase', {duration:1.4, easing: t => 1 - Math.pow(2, -10*t)})`.
  5. **Ingen `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` i klicket.** Behövs en mätning görs den i iframens
     `load` och vid resize, som i dag via `safeRefresh`.
- **Om iframen inte hunnit ladda vid klick:** casets skärmbild (`assets/cases/<case>-1440.webp`)
  står som affisch i ramen tills `load`. Därefter tonas iframen in på 0,3 s.
- Hopp direkt till `#showcase` utan val visar Calyx, som i V3f.

## B. Sajtens rörelse: `caseY` utan ryck

- Segment k (k = 1 … n−1) äger progressintervallet [k/n, (k+1)/n] och löper så här:
  - **första 50 %:** sajten glider från ankare k−1 till ankare k med `sine.inOut`. Hastigheten
    är noll i båda ändar, så inga ryck;
  - **sista 50 %:** sajten står still på ankare k, i läsfönstret.
  - Segment 0 är bara vila på ankare 0.
- Skrivningen behåller V3f:s `contentWindow.scrollTo({top:y, behavior:'instant'})` med
  0,5 px-tröskeln och drivs från ScrollTriggerns `onUpdate`. Ingen egen rAF-loop.
- **Experiment, bara om p95 i D inte nås:** flytta iframe-dokumentets rot med `transform` i
  stället för att scrolla. Mätt 2026-09-25: klientsajterna har `vh`-höjder (calyx.html:74,
  horai.html:157, 287) och en `position:fixed`-kornyta, så en iframe i full dokumenthöjd är
  utesluten. Välj inte experimentet utan mätning.

## C. Textrutan (ersätter dragspelet, bara desktop)

Högerkolumnens casehuvud (`.showcase-head`, rost/lack) står kvar. Under den ersätts
`.showcase-rows` av **en enda cell**, rutan, som fyller resterande höjd.

- **Rutans yta:** Calyx på `--paper`, svart text. Hōrai på `--black`, `--paper`-text och
  brödtext `#bdbdbd`. `padding: var(--cellpad)`, radie 0.
- **Överst i rutan:**
  - en mono-räknare `01 / 05`, uppdaterad när steget byts;
  - under den ett spår, 1 px svart linje (på Hōrai `--paper` på 30 %), där en 4 px mintfyllning
    skalas med `scaleX` kontinuerligt med pinnens progress, alltså alltid levande.
  - Båda är `aria-hidden="true"` (dekor, inte copy).
- **Stegen:** alla `h3` + `p` står staplade i samma gridcell (`display:grid` på behållaren,
  `grid-area:1/1` på varje steg), vertikalt centrerade i rutans resterande höjd.
  - `h3` behåller klassen `h3`, och `p` har samma text och `max-width:52ch`.
  - **Texten ändras inte med ett tecken.** Copy-diffen ska vara oförändrad.
- **Övertoningen** är en GSAP-tidslinje som skrubbas av samma pin via `onUpdate`, eller en
  tidslinje med `scrollTrigger` på samma trigger och `scrub:true`. Inte klass-toggle.
  - Steg k tonas ut i första 25 % av segment k+1 (`opacity 1→0`, `y 0→−12px`).
  - Steg k+1 tonas in i nästa 25 % (`opacity 0→1`, `y 12→0`).
  - Steget står helt still i resten av segmentet. Varje steg syns helt i ≥ 40 vh
    (75 vh × 75 %).
  - Bara `opacity` och `transform` animeras.
- **Tillgänglighet:** inaktiva steg får `aria-hidden="true"` och `visibility:hidden` när deras
  opacity är 0, så att skärmläsare och Tab bara når det synliga steget.
  - Växlingen görs i `onUpdate` när steget byts, inte per bildruta.
  - Under `prefers-reduced-motion` gäller F-011 (rörelse spelar alltid) som i V3f. Behåll V3f:s
    beteende.
- **Mobil (< 768):** V3f:s staplade rader under den sticky iframen behålls. Den aktiva raden står
  i opacity 1 och de andra i 0,45, med `opacity`-tween 0,35 s i `onEnter`/`onEnterBack`.
  Kontrast: 0,45 får inte ge brödtext under 4,5:1 — mät; höj till den nivå som klarar det.

## D. Verifiering (byggaren först, sedan leaden i pixlar)

Server: `python "C:/Users/Anton L/.agents/skills/design/scripts/serve.py" --port 3305 --root .`
från `C:\Users\Anton L\anti-slop-design`.

1. `python tests/alunix-r8/showcase_probe.py http://127.0.0.1:3305/tests/alunix-r8/runs/V3g/index.html tests/alunix-r8/runs/V3g/shots/probe-r1-1440 --width 1440 --headed`,
   och samma på 390. Jämför med `runs/V3f/shots/probe-baseline-*/result.json`. Krav:
   - p95 bildrutetid i klickfönstret och genom showcasen ≤ 20 ms, eller tydligt bättre än
     baslinjen om miljön inte når 20 ms;
   - största enskilda `scrollY`-hopp i klickfönstret under baslinjens;
   - `stall-then-lurch` = 0.
2. `python tests/alunix-r8/runs/V3g/verify_motion.py`, där `showcase_check` visar:
   - alla ankare ±2 px;
   - tangentbordsvägen (Tab till Hōrai, Enter);
   - hopp direkt till `#showcase`.
   Uppdatera kontrollen där den förutsätter dragspelets `is-active`-rader, så att den i stället
   läser vilket steg som syns i rutan.
3. `python tests/alunix-r8/runs/V3g/verify.py`: copy-diffen `passed: true`, 0 px överflöd vid
   390/768/1440/1920, 0 konsolfel.
4. Bildsekvensen efter klick (60/150/250/400/800/1400 ms) och `sheet.png` ur proben.
   `lead_motion_capture.py` 1440 och 390 mot board-cellen.
5. Rapportera siffrorna före och efter i `runs/V3g/RAPPORT.md`. Leaden läser bilderna själv.

Anton tog bort spärren och sessionen startades om med instruktionen att ladda `Skill(design)` på nytt och läsa exakt de filer nekningstexten räknade upp. Det gjordes i den ordningen: `design-catalogue/FEEDBACK.md` (katalogens egen fil, inte `skills/design/references/`- kopian jag hade läst första gången), `extract/*-design-language.md` för samtliga fyra valda katalogposter, `references/reference-lock.md`, `references/scroll/devices.md` och `references/scroll/feel-and-fingerprint.md` i `~/.agents/skills/design/` (den kanoniska sökvägen nekningen namngav, skild från repots egen `skills/design/`-kopia — innehållet visade sig identiskt vid jämförelse) samt fingerprint-registret `wiki/projects/_index/design-fingerprints.md`. Gaten släppte igenom nästa `Edit` utan ändringar i själva planen — research- och byggarbetet nedan är oförändrat av omstarten, bara ordningen på läsningen skiljer. ## Kedjan, steg för steg 1. **`Skill(design)`.** Läst i sin helhet (referensgolvets krav gäller varje steg, se ovan). Läst för referensgolvets skull, ingenting från dem syns i koden. `reference-lock.md`, `scroll/devices.md`, `scroll/feel-and-fingerprint.md` och fingerprint-registret lästa (se ovan). 2. **Inspo** (`references/inspo-mcp.md`). En `search_screens("sticky text column that crossfades step by step beside a scrolling product view")` → sex träffar, samtliga generiska hero-folds (Step, Warby Parker, Design Maestro, basement.studio, Superhuman, Tonal) — inspos index är foldautopsier av statiska sidor, ingen av dem visar en scroll-driven crossfade-mekanik. 413:### F-021 · En bra effekt försämrades av en ändring någon annanstans
414-- **Visades:** V3g R2 mot V3f. Tesrubriken "Det första intrycket är digitalt." var orörd i
415-  koden men märkbart mer statisk och ryckig.
416-- **Antons ord:** "var också bättre förra rundan, nu är den mer statisk och ryckig. Ta reda
417-  på anledningen … systemet får inte ta fel på bra effekter och göra de sämre, agenterna
418-  måste ha tydliga instruktioner och riktlinjer för vad som är bra."
419-- **Grundorsak (mätt):** iframes i en pinnad scen laddades om vid varje
420-  `ScrollTrigger.refresh()`, eftersom pin-spacern flyttar dem i DOM:en. Varje omladdning bad
421-  om en ny refresh, och loopen gick hela besöket: 6–12 omladdningar per iframe per pass.
422-  Felet fanns redan i V3f. R2 förladdade den andra sajten och dubblade kostnaden, och tesens
423-  p95 gick från 33 till 50–100 ms.
424-- **Regel:** godkända effekter skyddas. De står i körningens `EFFECTS.md` med en uppmätt
425-  signatur. Varje runda kör `section_probe.py` på HELA sidan mot baslinjen, och en sektion
426-  som blivit sämre blockerar rundan även om ingen rad i den ändrats. En iframe i en pin
427-  kräver en egen `pinSpacer`, och en refresh anropas aldrig från en iframes `load`.
428-- **Status:** `references/motion.md` § Approved effects are protected,

1	# The device kit, condensed
2	
3	Nine ways scroll can drive the page. Pick per beat, never per page: ≥4 device
4	families, never the same one twice running. Every act publishes `--sc-p` (0–1)
5	on itself, so bespoke CSS can ride the same value the kit devices use. Full
6	depth, worked examples, and every trap: `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/devices.md`.
7	
8	| # | Device | Syntax | Span / rate | One-line rule |
9	|---|---|---|---|---|
10	| 1 | `scrub` | `data-sc-act="scrub" data-sc-span="2.6" data-sc-dwell="0.35"` on the section; `data-sc-scrub data-sc-src="…"` on the `<video>` | span 2.2–3.0 for a hero | ≤2 per page. The wheel scrubs a pre-rendered clip; spend it on the open |
11	| 2 | `pin` | `data-sc-act="pin" data-sc-span="3"` | span ≥1.2 (below that, progress jumps 0→1 in one notch) | The frame holds, copy states cross over inside it |
12	| 3 | `pan` | `data-sc-act="pan" data-sc-span="3.2"`; rail gets `data-sc-pan="0.08"` | ~1vh per item + 1 | Lateral = breadth, not hierarchy. Overflow must be measured, not assumed |
13	| 4 | `reveal` | `data-sc-reveal="up|down|left|right|iris" data-sc-reveal-at="0.15 0.55"` | — | `clip-path` wipe = change of state. `iris` once per page at most |
14	| 5 | `kinetic` | `data-sc-kinetic="lines|words|chars"` on a cued heading | — | Lines almost always right, chars ~never. One kinetic headline per act |
15	| 6 | `parallax` | `data-sc-parallax="-0.6"` | rate is **hundreds of px total travel**, not a fraction — usable range 0.3–1.5 (framed), 1–2 (full-bleed) | Never on body copy. 3 layers is plenty |
16	| 7 | `count` | `data-sc-count="0 4,200" data-sc-count-at="0.1 0.5"` | 1.2–1.8s outside an act (`data-sc-count-ms`) | Only real numbers. No verified figure, no counter |
17	| 8 | `flow` + `in` | `data-sc-in data-sc-stagger="70"` on the wrap | stagger 30–80ms | The rest of the page. Fires once, opacity+14px rise, ~620ms ease-out |
18	| 9 | pointer: `tilt` / `magnet` / `spotlight` | `data-sc-tilt="7"` (5–9°), `data-sc-magnet="0.28"` (0.2–0.35, CTA only), `data-sc-spotlight` (publishes `--sc-mx`/`--sc-my`) | — | Gated to `(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`. Never gated on reduced motion (F-011, superseded 2026-09-07) |
19	
20	`drift` (`data-sc-drift="#0A0806"` on an act) is not a device, it's a
21	property: the page ground interpolates toward it while the act is live. 3–5
22	stops, one theme family. On a page of many *short* acts several can be
23	part-way through at once — paint grounds per section instead of drifting; see
24	upstream §10.
25	
26	## The engine: GSAP + Lenis (house default from 2026-09-24)
27	
28	**Every new build animates with GSAP** (+ScrollTrigger, SplitText when text is
29	split) **and Lenis.** Scrollcraft (`scripts/scroll/`) stays only for pages already
30	built on it — do not port an existing scrollcraft page to GSAP+Lenis just because
31	it's the new default. **Never mix the two engines on one page**: two scroll owners
32	is two RAF loops fighting for the same frame. Anton's instruction: GSAP+Lenis for
33	all animations, applied wherever the motion fits the design and elements of each
34	page.
35	
36	Vendored locally from `scripts/motion/vendor/` (gsap 3.15.0, ScrollTrigger,
37	SplitText, lenis 1.3.26 + `lenis.css`) — copy the whole folder into the build's
38	`assets/vendor/`; never a CDN at runtime. GSAP 3.13+ including SplitText is free.
39	
40	The init, verbatim — house deviations from Lenis's own defaults, each explained
41	once here so no builder reads the Lenis README and takes the default instead:
42	
43	```js
44	var lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: false, anchors: true, respectReducedMotion: false, lerp: 0.075, wheelMultiplier: 0.6 });
45	window.__lenis = lenis;
46	gsap.ticker.add(function (time) { lenis.raf(time * 1000); });
47	gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0);
48	lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update);
49	```
50	
51	- **`respectReducedMotion: false`.** Lenis's own default is `true`, which would
52	  silently switch off all motion for Anton, whose Windows runs with animation
53	  effects off (house rule F-011 / CARL design decision 2026-09-07). Rörelse spelar
54	  alltid — motion always plays.
55	- **`anchors: true`.** Lenis's default is `false`, which breaks in-page anchor
56	  links silently — no error, they just stop scrolling to the target.
57	- **`autoRaf: false`, driven by `gsap.ticker`.** `gsap.ticker` is the only RAF
58	  driver on the page; Lenis's own rAF loop would be a second one racing it.
59	- **`gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`** and **`lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)`**
60	  keep GSAP's tab-blur catch-up off and ScrollTrigger's cached positions synced to
61	  Lenis's virtual scroll on every frame.
62	- **`window.__lenis`** is the dev hook every jump-test drives:
63	  `lenis.scrollTo(el, {immediate:true})`, never `window.scrollTo`.
64	
65	No `scrollerProxy` (Lenis scrolls the real page, not a virtual container). No CSS
66	`scroll-behavior: smooth` anywhere — it fights Lenis's own smoothing.
67	
68	**Iframes.** `lenis.css` sets `pointer-events: none` on iframes while smooth-scroll
69	is active — wanted behaviour for scroll-driven embeds (a showcase iframe the reader
70	scrolls *past*). For an embed the reader should scroll *inside*, set
71	`data-lenis-prevent` on it.
72	
73	### Scrollcraft device → GSAP equivalent
74	
75	| Scrollcraft | GSAP + Lenis |
76	|---|---|
77	| `scrub` (`data-sc-act=scrub`) | ScrollTrigger `scrub: true` timeline |
78	| `pin` | `pin: true`, created **once** at init |
79	| `pan` | pinned timeline, `xPercent` |
80	| `reveal` | `ScrollTrigger.batch` or a per-element trigger, fail toward visible |
81	| `kinetic` | SplitText `type:'lines,words,chars', mask:'lines'` + per-word `white-space: nowrap`; the mask needs `padding-bottom` with an equal negative margin so descenders survive |
82	| `parallax` | `yPercent` scrub |
83	| `count` | tween on a plain object + `snap` / `gsap.utils.snap` |
84	| `tilt` / `magnet` | `gsap.quickTo`, gated `(hover: hover)` |
85	| grid dissolve | `stagger: {grid, from:'random'}` |
86	| `responsive` (`gsap.matchMedia`) | `gsap.matchMedia()` |
87	
88	### Load-bearing rules
89	
90	- Create every ScrollTrigger **in page order.**
91	- **Never mix `scrub` and `toggleActions` on one trigger.**
92	- The **last element on the page** uses `end: 'bottom bottom'`.
93	- **With Lenis, use `scrub: true`, not a numeric scrub.** Lenis is the ONE
94	  smoothing layer on the page — a numeric scrub value stacks a second lag on top
95	  of it. Measured jank in V3f's showcase, 2026-09-24.
96	- **A pin is created once at init and is never killed/recreated on user
97	  interaction.** V3f's click handler did that and produced a hard, visible
98	  transition where the pin snapped instead of holding.
99	- **`end` is set in pixels via a function, with `invalidateOnRefresh: true` —
100	  never a `'+=Nvh'` string.** ScrollTrigger silently ignores the `vh` suffix on
101	  that shorthand — measured V3f R5.
102	
103	- **An iframe inside a pinned element needs an explicit `pinSpacer`.** ScrollTrigger re-parents
104	  the pinned element into its own pin-spacer on every `refresh()`, and a re-parented iframe
105	  reloads its document. If that iframe's `load` then asks for a refresh, the page runs a
106	  reload loop for the whole visit (measured Alunix V3f/V3g 2026-09-25: 6–12 reloads per
107	  iframe per pass, ~1/s, and the thesis headline two sections away lost half its frames).
108	  Put a wrapper in the markup (`<div class="x-pin-spacer"><div class="x-stage">…`) and pass
109	  `pinSpacer: '.x-pin-spacer'`. Never call `refresh()` from an iframe's `load`; an iframe
110	  has fixed dimensions and cannot change the outer layout.
111	- **Every scrubbed trigger uses `scrub: true`** — hero and thesis pins included, not only
112	  the one being edited this round. A numeric scrub anywhere is a second smoothing layer.
113	- **House pace (Anton 2026-09-25: "scrollen går för snabbt … man kastas förbi kortet").**
114	  Lenis `wheelMultiplier: 0.6` and `lerp: 0.075` — one wheel notch moves ~60 px and glides.
115	  A pin whose content the reader must watch happen (a card flip, a step change) spans at
116	  least 200 vh of scroll; nothing the reader should see may complete within one or two
117	  notches. Slower is only better if it stays even: verify with `section_probe.py`.
118	- **Check: `scripts/section_probe.py URL --baseline <previous.json>`** after every round,
119	  on the WHOLE page, not only the edited section. It fails on an iframe that loads more
120	  than once, on any refresh during the scroll pass, and on any section whose p95 frame time
121	  got worse than the approved baseline. Verified to fail on V3f and V3g before the fix.
122	
123	### Skills to load before the first line of motion code
124	
125	In order: `lenis` → `gsap-core` → `gsap-scrolltrigger` → `gsap-timeline` →
126	`gsap-plugins` (if SplitText/Flip) → `gsap-performance` → `gsap-utils` (if
127	needed). Plus the UI-skills registry's `ibelick/fixing-motion-performance` — see
128	[`skill-orchestration.md`](../skill-orchestration.md).
129	
130	## The cue contract — what verification actually catches you on
131	
132	`data-sc-cue="from [to [rampIn [rampOut]]]"`, all in act progress 0–1.
133	
134	| Form | Behaviour |
135	|---|---|
136	| `"0.2"` | fades in at 0.2, **holds to the end of the act** |
137	| `"0.1 0.6"` | in, plateau, out (ramps default 30% of window each) |
138	| `"0 0.78 0"` | **greet**: full opacity at act start, then fades — the hero form |
139	| `"0 1 0 0"` | **greet and hold**: full at p=0, no ramp either end |
140	
141	**The plateau is the point.** Without one, a cue is a triangle that touches full
142	opacity for a single instant, so the reader has to stop on exactly the right
143	pixel to see the line at full strength and every heading reads slightly faded.
144	`"0.1 0.9 0.15 0.4"` — fast in, long slow out — is the confident form. Cue
145	windows on a pinned act **overlap by design**, roughly 15% of the act: the
146	outgoing line is still fading while the next arrives, and a gap between cues
147	reads as a loading failure.
148	
149	Five rules, each one a real bug this fixture has caught:
150	
151	- **A hero cue needs the greet form.** A plain `"0 0.7"` means the first
152	  screen every visitor sees has no headline on it.
153	- **The last act's cue must hold** (one value). A two-value close cue fades
154	  the CTA out before the page ends.
155	- **Only the last act may hold.** A one-value cue on a *middle* pinned act
156	  stays lit through the whole un-pin slide — the line travels a full viewport
157	  up, crosses fixed chrome, overlaps the next section. Invisible until
158	  measured; shows up as a contrast failure nobody meant.
159	- **Ground or greet.** A pinned stage is fully visible ~1vh *before* its own
160	  progress leaves 0. A plain two-value first cue shows an empty stage for
161	  that whole travel — give the act a ground (image/colour already doing
162	  work) or open with a greet cue.
163	- **Clip time ≠ cue time.** A `scrub` clip is mapped across the stage's
164	  *entire visible life* (default), not across the pinned travel, because the
165	  stage is on screen for a viewport before the pin starts and after it ends.
166	  Cues keep using `p` (they belong to the pin); the clip uses a separately
167	  computed `vp`. Reaching for `data-sc-clip-map="travel"` reintroduces the
168	  freeze — there's almost no reason to.
169	
170	Two more that a harness will not catch by itself:
171	
172	- **Pan overflow must be measured, not assumed.** The rail travels exactly
173	  `scrollWidth - viewport`; a rail narrower than the viewport travels **zero**
174	  and the act reads as a still. `rail.scrollWidth - innerWidth` — check it,
175	  don't guess.
176	- **Parallax rate is hundreds of pixels total, not a viewport fraction** — see
177	  the table above. A rate of 0.35 across three viewport-heights of scroll is
178	  35px: invisible.
179	
180	Composing an act: devices stack (a pinned stage can hold a scrub clip, a
181	parallax layer, a kinetic headline, a spotlight at once), but one thing is the
182	reason the act exists — say that thing in one sentence or the act has none.
183	
184	## The playhead is lerped (§1)
185	
186	The mechanism the whole kit's smoothness rests on, and the one F-012 kept
187	being blamed on. **Scroll never writes `currentTime`.** It writes a *target*,
188	and a standalone rAF loop walks the clip toward that target at a fixed
189	fraction per frame:
190	
191	> *"Wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate, so a 1:1 write reproduces
192	> every gap in them and the clip reads as a stutter rather than a glide."*
193	
194	Three mechanisms, all on by default:
195	
196	- **Lerp 0.18 per frame.** `data-sc-lerp` overrides it, on the mount root for
197	  the whole page or on a single `<video>`. **Clamped to 0.02–1 and never read
198	  as 0** — a 0 lerp is a playhead that never moves. Reach for an override only
199	  when a page's clips are short enough that 0.18 visibly lags the hand.
200	  Worldflight wants 0.12 instead; see [`pace.md`](pace.md).
201	- **Deadband: 8 ms desktop, 20 ms mobile.** A write smaller than that costs a
202	  seek and shows nothing; on a phone it costs more than it shows.
203	- **Seek coalescing.** No seek is queued while the decoder is still resolving
204	  the last one. *"A fast flick otherwise piles seeks up and freezes the clip."*
205	
206	An offscreen clip that has already reached its target stops being touched at
207	all. (Upstream states the offscreen skip without a threshold value; the 0.002
208	figure belongs to `shoot.mjs`'s settle test, below, not to this skip.)
209	
210	This applies to **every** scrub clip on the page, act or worldflight. It is
211	also why the shooter waits for the playhead to arrive before each frame:
212	
213	> *"A frame captured mid-lerp is a frame the page never actually holds."*
214	
215	`shoot.mjs` settles on `|current − target| < 0.002 && !seeking`. Any harness
216	the chain runs against a scrubbed page inherits that requirement — a
217	screenshot taken mid-lerp makes the run unrepeatable, not merely imprecise.
218	
219	Upstream also drops the damping to 1.0 (no smoothing at all) under reduced
220	motion. **That branch does not port: F-011.** The lerp is unconditional here,
221	which is the correct behaviour anyway — it is a smoothing mechanism, not an
222	effect, and turning it off is what produces the stepping fault.
223	
224	## Layered scenes: where the premium feel comes from (§6)
225	
226	Ported from `devices.md` § 6, measured off a reference premium site and proven
227	on a live build. A flat page moves as one sheet; a layered page is a stack of
228	cut-out planes sliding past each other, and *"the eye reads that differential
229	motion as depth before it reads anything else."* It is the single biggest
230	difference between a page that feels built and one that feels assembled, and
231	it costs three transparent images and a multiplier each.
232	
233	- **Plan the planes back to front.** Far ridge, mid ridge, the product, then a
234	  **foreground plane in front of the product**. The product sits between mid
235	  and front, so the foreground overtakes it as the reader scrolls. That
236	  overtaking is the move.
237	- **Small rate differences, not big ones.** The reference hero lags the far
238	  plane **31%** behind the page, the mid plane **17%**, the product **20%**,
239	  and foreground and copy travel at exactly **1×**. Adjacent planes differ by
240	  **10–30%**. Larger stops reading as distance and starts reading as things
241	  sliding around. **Copy always rides at 1×.**
242	- **Shape the foreground for the product.** A straight-edged foreground covers
243	  the product's CTA within a few hundred pixels of scroll. Cut it so it dips
244	  where the product is and rises at the edges, and the button stays in view
245	  two to three times as long.
246	- **Every plane is solid below its silhouette.** Cut-out art that fades to
247	  transparent at the bottom lets the plane behind show through as the planes
248	  separate. Fill each column solid from its first opaque pixel down.
249	- **Fade the section floor.** Planes travel past the section's bottom edge and
250	  are clipped there. A gradient to the page ground over the last 200–300 px,
251	  layered above every plane, hides the clip line at any scroll position.
252	
253	Three traps, each of which cost a round of fixes:
254	
255	- A global `img { max-width: 100% }` shrinks an absolutely positioned plane to
256	  the viewport on phones, so the far layer never shows. **Planes carry
257	  `max-width: none` and a fixed pixel width.**
258	- **Never `transition: transform` on a parallaxed element.** A reveal class is
259	  the usual culprit. The transition eases every per-frame scroll write over
260	  its own duration, and on a phone that reads as the product lagging a full
261	  second behind the thumb. Parallaxed elements transition **opacity only**.
262	- Replacing a plane's art under the same filename ships nothing to a phone
263	  holding the old bytes. **New art gets a new name.**
264	
265	`data-sc-parallax` and a raw scroll multiplier are the same tool in different
266	units. What matters is the **ratio between planes**, not the absolute travel.
267	
268	## The premium fade-in, exactly (§8)
269	
270	The `flow` + `in` device is most of the page, so its defaults decide how the
271	page feels between the acts:
272	
273	| Ingredient | Value |
274	|---|---|
275	| Opacity | 0 → 1 |
276	| Rise | **~14 px** |
277	| Duration | **~620 ms**, ease-out |
278	| Stagger | **30–80 ms**, children in reading order |
279	| Trigger | IntersectionObserver, `-12%` bottom root margin, **fires once** |
280	
281	- **A fade with no rise reads as a loading glitch.** A rise **past 24 px reads
282	  as a slide.** 14 px is the band, not a starting point to tune upward.
283	- The `-12%` margin fires the reveal when the reader is looking, not when the
284	  first pixel clears the fold.
285	- `data-sc-in` is what the engine watches. Without it nothing fires and the
286	  stagger children stay hidden.
287	- **Content that re-hides on the way back up is a defect, not an effect.**
288	- *"Larger, slower, or bouncier is never more premium; the restraint is the
289	  signal."*
290	
291	**A flow section directly after a pinned act takes reduced padding.** The
292	pinned stage needs a full viewport to scroll off, and full `--sc-section`
293	padding on top of that delays the flow section's first content by another
294	screen. The harness will not call it dead scroll — correctly, the stage is
295	moving — and the reader still sees a near-empty screen. Cut the block padding
296	there and start the first reveal near `p = 0`.
297	
298	## Rail settle on `pan` (§3)
299	
300	Lateral travel alone reads as a slideshow on rails. **Give the rail's items a
301	staggered settle driven from `--sc-p`** and they read as a drawer being
302	pulled instead.
303	
304	- **Exempt the first item** — a `pan` act needs its opening content already
305	  present.
306	- **Floor the opacity around 0.55**, so a not-yet-settled card reads as
307	  arriving rather than as failing to load.
308	
309	Upstream gates the settle to `prefers-reduced-motion` — **utgår, F-011**.
310	The settle always runs. What *does* survive from
311	the same passage is the reachability requirement, which is not a motion
312	preference at all: a `pan` rail's transform **is** the navigation, so nothing
313	may zero it and park the act on its first screenful. Every item in a rail
314	stays reachable, and that is checked on the sheet, not assumed.
315	
316	Two more, from the same section:
317	
318	- **Card copy is read while cropped.** Items enter and leave through the
319	  viewport edges, so a heading is half-shown for most of its life, and two
320	  half-headings side by side can read as a third word (`TRACE` beside
321	  `EVALUATE` becoming `RE EVALUATE`). Keep card headings to one or two short
322	  words and expect every line to be read partially cut off.
323	- If three items do not reach half a viewport of overflow, **the fix is more
324	  rail, not wider cards**: put the act's heading in as the first item and a
325	  closing note as the last. Both earn their place, and they add the width the
326	  travel needs.
327	
328	## Devices that cannot share an element (§9)
329	
330	**`magnet`, `parallax` and `cue` all write `transform`.** The magnet writes
331	every frame in its own rAF loop, so it silently wins and the cue's entrance
332	rise is discarded — a visible animation lost to a race, with nothing in the
333	console.
334	
335	- On a magnetic CTA, set **`data-sc-rise="0"`** so the cue writes a no-op
336	  instead of losing to the magnet.
337	- A cued element that wants its own continuous transform drives an **inner
338	  wrapper** from `--sc-p` in CSS, rather than stacking a second device on the
339	  same node.
340	
341	All three pointer devices **interpolate toward** the pointer rather than
342	tracking it directly: *"direct tracking reads as artificial because it carries
343	no momentum."* They stay gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so
344	touch never fires a false hover — that gate is a pointer-capability query, not
345	a motion preference, and it stands.
346	The reduced-motion half of the same sentence does not port (F-011).
347	
348	## Kinetic type: the mask and the re-split (§5)
349	
350	Each unit slides up from **behind a mask**, so it enters from a clean edge
351	rather than simply fading.
352	
353	- **Line masks must reserve room for descenders.** A mask clipped to the line
354	  box shears the tails off g, y, p and j, *"and that is the single most common
355	  way this effect looks broken."*
356	- **Line splitting measures real line boxes, so it re-runs after
357	  `document.fonts.ready`.** Do not call it on text still loading its face. The
358	  same `fonts.ready` handle earns its place twice over: a webfont swapping in
359	  changes the measured height of every copy block, so anything sized against
360	  those blocks (a scrim plate, a rail) is wrong until it re-measures.
361	- Lines are almost always right; words for a short punch line; characters
362	  approximately never, *"because it turns reading into waiting."*
363	- **One kinetic headline per act, at most.**
364	
365	## What makes a `count` land (§7)
366	
367	- **Ease out, hard.** A cubic ease-out, so most of the distance goes by in the
368	  first third and the last digits settle slowly. *"A linear count reads as a
369	  slot machine."*
370	- **1.2–1.8 s.** Under a second and the reader misses that it moved; past two
371	  and they are waiting for a number they have already guessed.
372	- **Fires at half visibility, once**, so the reader is looking at it when it
373	  starts, and it never re-runs on the way back up.
374	- **Pair it with the fade.** A counter inside a `data-sc-in` stack rises in
375	  with its label and starts ticking as it arrives — *"the same numbers static
376	  on the page read as a spreadsheet."*
377	- Write the target exactly as it should render, commas included; the engine
378	  strips them before parsing and applies `tabular-nums` so the layout does not
379	  jitter.
380	
381	**A concept, fictional or pre-launch brand has no verified figures, so it has
382	no counters.** The device suits a SaaS or agency page and will look good in
383	the score table, *"which is exactly the trap: every number you could put in it
384	would be invented."* Decide this before designing an act around a number, not
385	after. Real brand, real stats, or a different device.
386	
387	## Appendix: pattern vocabulary
388	
389	Named patterns from taste-skill § 10, carried here so orchestrator, builder
390	and reviewer name the same thing. It is a **vocabulary, not a menu** — several
391	entries below are banned as directions elsewhere in the chain (glassmorphism,
392	holographic foil, carousels, gooey menus) and appear here only so a critique
393	can say which trope it is refusing.
394	
395	- **Hero** — Asymmetric Split · Editorial Manifesto · Video/Media Mask ·
396	  Kinetic-Type · Curtain-Reveal · Scroll-Pinned.
397	- **Nav** — Dock Magnification · Magnetic Button (`data-sc-magnet`) · Gooey
398	  Menu · Dynamic Island · Contextual Radial · Floating Speed Dial · Mega Menu
399	  Reveal.
400	- **Layout** — Bento Grid · Masonry · Chroma Grid · Split-Screen Scroll ·
401	  Sticky-Stack Sections.
402	- **Cards** — Parallax Tilt Card (`data-sc-tilt`) · Spotlight Border Card
403	  (`data-sc-spotlight`) · Glassmorphism Panel · Holographic Foil ·
404	  Tinder Swipe Stack · Morphing Modal.
405	- **Scroll** — Sticky Scroll Stack · Horizontal Scroll Hijack (= `pan`) ·
406	  Locomotive / Sequence Scroll (= `scrub`) · Zoom Parallax · Scroll Progress
407	  Path · Liquid Swipe Transition.
408	- **Galleries** — Dome Gallery · Coverflow Carousel · Drag-to-Pan Grid ·
409	  Accordion Image Slider · Hover Image Trail · Glitch Effect Image.
410	- **Type** — Kinetic Marquee · **Text Mask Reveal** (massive type as a
411	  transparent window onto video — this is K2's letter-window) · Text Scramble
412	  · Circular Text Path · Gradient Stroke Animation · Kinetic Typography Grid.
413	- **Micro** — Particle Explosion Button · Liquid Pull-to-Refresh · Skeleton
414	  Shimmer · Directional Hover-Aware Button · Ripple Click · Animated SVG Line
415	  Drawing · Mesh Gradient Background · Lens Blur Depth.
416	
417	Names alone are not permission. A pattern still has to clear the fingerprint
418	gate, the register, and `../motion.md` before it ships.
419	
420	## Never restyle the engine's classes (AB06, 2026-09-03)
421	
422	Theme the engine only through its six colour tokens and two fonts. A project rule on
423	`.sc-stage`, `.sc-copy`, `.sc-scrim` or any other `.sc-*` class silently wins over the
424	engine: the console then says `[scrollcraft] act "…" will not pin: its stage computes
425	position:relative` and every pinned act scrolls away, leaving its spacer as dead scroll.
426	Read the console for `[scrollcraft]` warnings before anything else in Step 5, and run
427	`scripts/scroll_verify.py` — a blind one-shot cannot see either. The engine is opt-in per
428	grammar (scrub, pin, pan); a page that keeps the chain's own single set-piece + shared
429	reveal does not need it.

# The device kit, condensed

Nine ways scroll can drive the page. Pick per beat, never per page: ≥4 device
families, never the same one twice running. Every act publishes `--sc-p` (0–1)
on itself, so bespoke CSS can ride the same value the kit devices use. Full
depth, worked examples, and every trap: `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/devices.md`.

| # | Device | Syntax | Span / rate | One-line rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scrub` | `data-sc-act="scrub" data-sc-span="2.6" data-sc-dwell="0.35"` on the section; `data-sc-scrub data-sc-src="…"` on the `<video>` | span 2.2–3.0 for a hero | ≤2 per page. The wheel scrubs a pre-rendered clip; spend it on the open |
| 2 | `pin` | `data-sc-act="pin" data-sc-span="3"` | span ≥1.2 (below that, progress jumps 0→1 in one notch) | The frame holds, copy states cross over inside it |
| 3 | `pan` | `data-sc-act="pan" data-sc-span="3.2"`; rail gets `data-sc-pan="0.08"` | ~1vh per item + 1 | Lateral = breadth, not hierarchy. Overflow must be measured, not assumed |
| 4 | `reveal` | `data-sc-reveal="up|down|left|right|iris" data-sc-reveal-at="0.15 0.55"` | — | `clip-path` wipe = change of state. `iris` once per page at most |
| 5 | `kinetic` | `data-sc-kinetic="lines|words|chars"` on a cued heading | — | Lines almost always right, chars ~never. One kinetic headline per act |
| 6 | `parallax` | `data-sc-parallax="-0.6"` | rate is **hundreds of px total travel**, not a fraction — usable range 0.3–1.5 (framed), 1–2 (full-bleed) | Never on body copy. 3 layers is plenty |
| 7 | `count` | `data-sc-count="0 4,200" data-sc-count-at="0.1 0.5"` | 1.2–1.8s outside an act (`data-sc-count-ms`) | Only real numbers. No verified figure, no counter |
| 8 | `flow` + `in` | `data-sc-in data-sc-stagger="70"` on the wrap | stagger 30–80ms | The rest of the page. Fires once, opacity+14px rise, ~620ms ease-out |
| 9 | pointer: `tilt` / `magnet` / `spotlight` | `data-sc-tilt="7"` (5–9°), `data-sc-magnet="0.28"` (0.2–0.35, CTA only), `data-sc-spotlight` (publishes `--sc-mx`/`--sc-my`) | — | Gated to `(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`. Never gated on reduced motion (F-011, superseded 2026-09-07) |

`drift` (`data-sc-drift="#0A0806"` on an act) is not a device, it's a
property: the page ground interpolates toward it while the act is live. 3–5
stops, one theme family. On a page of many *short* acts several can be
part-way through at once — paint grounds per section instead of drifting; see
upstream §10.

## The engine: GSAP + Lenis (house default from 2026-09-24)

**Every new build animates with GSAP** (+ScrollTrigger, SplitText when text is
split) **and Lenis.** Scrollcraft (`scripts/scroll/`) stays only for pages already
built on it — do not port an existing scrollcraft page to GSAP+Lenis just because
it's the new default. **Never mix the two engines on one page**: two scroll owners
is two RAF loops fighting for the same frame. Anton's instruction: GSAP+Lenis for
all animations, applied wherever the motion fits the design and elements of each
page.

Vendored locally from `scripts/motion/vendor/` (gsap 3.15.0, ScrollTrigger,
SplitText, lenis 1.3.26 + `lenis.css`) — copy the whole folder into the build's
`assets/vendor/`; never a CDN at runtime. GSAP 3.13+ including SplitText is free.

The init, verbatim — house deviations from Lenis's own defaults, each explained
once here so no builder reads the Lenis README and takes the default instead:

```js
var lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: false, anchors: true, respectReducedMotion: false, lerp: 0.075, wheelMultiplier: 0.6 });
window.__lenis = lenis;
gsap.ticker.add(function (time) { lenis.raf(time * 1000); });
gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0);
lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update);
```

- **`respectReducedMotion: false`.** Lenis's own default is `true`, which would
  silently switch off all motion for Anton, whose Windows runs with animation
  effects off (house rule F-011 / CARL design decision 2026-09-07). Rörelse spelar
  alltid — motion always plays.
- **`anchors: true`.** Lenis's default is `false`, which breaks in-page anchor
  links silently — no error, they just stop scrolling to the target.
- **`autoRaf: false`, driven by `gsap.ticker`.** `gsap.ticker` is the only RAF
  driver on the page; Lenis's own rAF loop would be a second one racing it.
- **`gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`** and **`lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)`**
  keep GSAP's tab-blur catch-up off and ScrollTrigger's cached positions synced to
  Lenis's virtual scroll on every frame.
- **`window.__lenis`** is the dev hook every jump-test drives:
  `lenis.scrollTo(el, {immediate:true})`, never `window.scrollTo`.

No `scrollerProxy` (Lenis scrolls the real page, not a virtual container). No CSS
`scroll-behavior: smooth` anywhere — it fights Lenis's own smoothing.

**Iframes.** `lenis.css` sets `pointer-events: none` on iframes while smooth-scroll
is active — wanted behaviour for scroll-driven embeds (a showcase iframe the reader
scrolls *past*). For an embed the reader should scroll *inside*, set
`data-lenis-prevent` on it.

### Scrollcraft device → GSAP equivalent

| Scrollcraft | GSAP + Lenis |
|---|---|
| `scrub` (`data-sc-act=scrub`) | ScrollTrigger `scrub: true` timeline |
| `pin` | `pin: true`, created **once** at init |
| `pan` | pinned timeline, `xPercent` |
| `reveal` | `ScrollTrigger.batch` or a per-element trigger, fail toward visible |
| `kinetic` | SplitText `type:'lines,words,chars', mask:'lines'` + per-word `white-space: nowrap`; the mask needs `padding-bottom` with an equal negative margin so descenders survive |
| `parallax` | `yPercent` scrub |
| `count` | tween on a plain object + `snap` / `gsap.utils.snap` |
| `tilt` / `magnet` | `gsap.quickTo`, gated `(hover: hover)` |
| grid dissolve | `stagger: {grid, from:'random'}` |
| `responsive` (`gsap.matchMedia`) | `gsap.matchMedia()` |

### Load-bearing rules

- Create every ScrollTrigger **in page order.**
- **Never mix `scrub` and `toggleActions` on one trigger.**
- The **last element on the page** uses `end: 'bottom bottom'`.
- **With Lenis, use `scrub: true`, not a numeric scrub.** Lenis is the ONE
  smoothing layer on the page — a numeric scrub value stacks a second lag on top
  of it. Measured jank in V3f's showcase, 2026-09-24.
- **A pin is created once at init and is never killed/recreated on user
  interaction.** V3f's click handler did that and produced a hard, visible
  transition where the pin snapped instead of holding.
- **`end` is set in pixels via a function, with `invalidateOnRefresh: true` —
  never a `'+=Nvh'` string.** ScrollTrigger silently ignores the `vh` suffix on
  that shorthand — measured V3f R5.

- **An iframe inside a pinned element needs an explicit `pinSpacer`.** ScrollTrigger re-parents
  the pinned element into its own pin-spacer on every `refresh()`, and a re-parented iframe
  reloads its document. If that iframe's `load` then asks for a refresh, the page runs a
  reload loop for the whole visit (measured Alunix V3f/V3g 2026-09-25: 6–12 reloads per
  iframe per pass, ~1/s, and the thesis headline two sections away lost half its frames).
  Put a wrapper in the markup (`<div class="x-pin-spacer"><div class="x-stage">…`) and pass
  `pinSpacer: '.x-pin-spacer'`. Never call `refresh()` from an iframe's `load`; an iframe
  has fixed dimensions and cannot change the outer layout.
- **Every scrubbed trigger uses `scrub: true`** — hero and thesis pins included, not only
  the one being edited this round. A numeric scrub anywhere is a second smoothing layer.
- **House pace (Anton 2026-09-25: "scrollen går för snabbt … man kastas förbi kortet").**
  Lenis `wheelMultiplier: 0.6` and `lerp: 0.075` — one wheel notch moves ~60 px and glides.
  A pin whose content the reader must watch happen (a card flip, a step change) spans at
  least 200 vh of scroll; nothing the reader should see may complete within one or two
  notches. Slower is only better if it stays even: verify with `section_probe.py`.
- **Check: `scripts/section_probe.py URL --baseline <previous.json>`** after every round,
  on the WHOLE page, not only the edited section. It fails on an iframe that loads more
  than once, on any refresh during the scroll pass, and on any section whose p95 frame time
  got worse than the approved baseline. Verified to fail on V3f and V3g before the fix.

### Skills to load before the first line of motion code

In order: `lenis` → `gsap-core` → `gsap-scrolltrigger` → `gsap-timeline` →
`gsap-plugins` (if SplitText/Flip) → `gsap-performance` → `gsap-utils` (if
needed). Plus the UI-skills registry's `ibelick/fixing-motion-performance` — see
[`skill-orchestration.md`](../skill-orchestration.md).

## The cue contract — what verification actually catches you on

`data-sc-cue="from [to [rampIn [rampOut]]]"`, all in act progress 0–1.

| Form | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `"0.2"` | fades in at 0.2, **holds to the end of the act** |
| `"0.1 0.6"` | in, plateau, out (ramps default 30% of window each) |
| `"0 0.78 0"` | **greet**: full opacity at act start, then fades — the hero form |
| `"0 1 0 0"` | **greet and hold**: full at p=0, no ramp either end |

**The plateau is the point.** Without one, a cue is a triangle that touches full
opacity for a single instant, so the reader has to stop on exactly the right
pixel to see the line at full strength and every heading reads slightly faded.
`"0.1 0.9 0.15 0.4"` — fast in, long slow out — is the confident form. Cue
windows on a pinned act **overlap by design**, roughly 15% of the act: the
outgoing line is still fading while the next arrives, and a gap between cues
reads as a loading failure.

Five rules, each one a real bug this fixture has caught:

- **A hero cue needs the greet form.** A plain `"0 0.7"` means the first
  screen every visitor sees has no headline on it.
- **The last act's cue must hold** (one value). A two-value close cue fades
  the CTA out before the page ends.
- **Only the last act may hold.** A one-value cue on a *middle* pinned act
  stays lit through the whole un-pin slide — the line travels a full viewport
  up, crosses fixed chrome, overlaps the next section. Invisible until
  measured; shows up as a contrast failure nobody meant.
- **Ground or greet.** A pinned stage is fully visible ~1vh *before* its own
  progress leaves 0. A plain two-value first cue shows an empty stage for
  that whole travel — give the act a ground (image/colour already doing
  work) or open with a greet cue.
- **Clip time ≠ cue time.** A `scrub` clip is mapped across the stage's
  *entire visible life* (default), not across the pinned travel, because the
  stage is on screen for a viewport before the pin starts and after it ends.
  Cues keep using `p` (they belong to the pin); the clip uses a separately
  computed `vp`. Reaching for `data-sc-clip-map="travel"` reintroduces the
  freeze — there's almost no reason to.

Two more that a harness will not catch by itself:

- **Pan overflow must be measured, not assumed.** The rail travels exactly
  `scrollWidth - viewport`; a rail narrower than the viewport travels **zero**
  and the act reads as a still. `rail.scrollWidth - innerWidth` — check it,
  don't guess.
- **Parallax rate is hundreds of pixels total, not a viewport fraction** — see
  the table above. A rate of 0.35 across three viewport-heights of scroll is
  35px: invisible.

Composing an act: devices stack (a pinned stage can hold a scrub clip, a
parallax layer, a kinetic headline, a spotlight at once), but one thing is the
reason the act exists — say that thing in one sentence or the act has none.

## The playhead is lerped (§1)

The mechanism the whole kit's smoothness rests on, and the one F-012 kept
being blamed on. **Scroll never writes `currentTime`.** It writes a *target*,
and a standalone rAF loop walks the clip toward that target at a fixed
fraction per frame:

> *"Wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate, so a 1:1 write reproduces
> every gap in them and the clip reads as a stutter rather than a glide."*

Three mechanisms, all on by default:

- **Lerp 0.18 per frame.** `data-sc-lerp` overrides it, on the mount root for
  the whole page or on a single `<video>`. **Clamped to 0.02–1 and never read
  as 0** — a 0 lerp is a playhead that never moves. Reach for an override only
  when a page's clips are short enough that 0.18 visibly lags the hand.
  Worldflight wants 0.12 instead; see [`pace.md`](pace.md).
- **Deadband: 8 ms desktop, 20 ms mobile.** A write smaller than that costs a
  seek and shows nothing; on a phone it costs more than it shows.
- **Seek coalescing.** No seek is queued while the decoder is still resolving
  the last one. *"A fast flick otherwise piles seeks up and freezes the clip."*

An offscreen clip that has already reached its target stops being touched at
all. (Upstream states the offscreen skip without a threshold value; the 0.002
figure belongs to `shoot.mjs`'s settle test, below, not to this skip.)

This applies to **every** scrub clip on the page, act or worldflight. It is
also why the shooter waits for the playhead to arrive before each frame:

> *"A frame captured mid-lerp is a frame the page never actually holds."*

`shoot.mjs` settles on `|current − target| < 0.002 && !seeking`. Any harness
the chain runs against a scrubbed page inherits that requirement — a
screenshot taken mid-lerp makes the run unrepeatable, not merely imprecise.

Upstream also drops the damping to 1.0 (no smoothing at all) under reduced
motion. **That branch does not port: F-011.** The lerp is unconditional here,
which is the correct behaviour anyway — it is a smoothing mechanism, not an
effect, and turning it off is what produces the stepping fault.

## Layered scenes: where the premium feel comes from (§6)

Ported from `devices.md` § 6, measured off a reference premium site and proven
on a live build. A flat page moves as one sheet; a layered page is a stack of
cut-out planes sliding past each other, and *"the eye reads that differential
motion as depth before it reads anything else."* It is the single biggest
difference between a page that feels built and one that feels assembled, and
it costs three transparent images and a multiplier each.

- **Plan the planes back to front.** Far ridge, mid ridge, the product, then a
  **foreground plane in front of the product**. The product sits between mid
  and front, so the foreground overtakes it as the reader scrolls. That
  overtaking is the move.
- **Small rate differences, not big ones.** The reference hero lags the far
  plane **31%** behind the page, the mid plane **17%**, the product **20%**,
  and foreground and copy travel at exactly **1×**. Adjacent planes differ by
  **10–30%**. Larger stops reading as distance and starts reading as things
  sliding around. **Copy always rides at 1×.**
- **Shape the foreground for the product.** A straight-edged foreground covers
  the product's CTA within a few hundred pixels of scroll. Cut it so it dips
  where the product is and rises at the edges, and the button stays in view
  two to three times as long.
- **Every plane is solid below its silhouette.** Cut-out art that fades to
  transparent at the bottom lets the plane behind show through as the planes
  separate. Fill each column solid from its first opaque pixel down.
- **Fade the section floor.** Planes travel past the section's bottom edge and
  are clipped there. A gradient to the page ground over the last 200–300 px,
  layered above every plane, hides the clip line at any scroll position.

Three traps, each of which cost a round of fixes:

- A global `img { max-width: 100% }` shrinks an absolutely positioned plane to
  the viewport on phones, so the far layer never shows. **Planes carry
  `max-width: none` and a fixed pixel width.**
- **Never `transition: transform` on a parallaxed element.** A reveal class is
  the usual culprit. The transition eases every per-frame scroll write over
  its own duration, and on a phone that reads as the product lagging a full
  second behind the thumb. Parallaxed elements transition **opacity only**.
- Replacing a plane's art under the same filename ships nothing to a phone
  holding the old bytes. **New art gets a new name.**

`data-sc-parallax` and a raw scroll multiplier are the same tool in different
units. What matters is the **ratio between planes**, not the absolute travel.

## The premium fade-in, exactly (§8)

The `flow` + `in` device is most of the page, so its defaults decide how the
page feels between the acts:

| Ingredient | Value |
|---|---|
| Opacity | 0 → 1 |
| Rise | **~14 px** |
| Duration | **~620 ms**, ease-out |
| Stagger | **30–80 ms**, children in reading order |
| Trigger | IntersectionObserver, `-12%` bottom root margin, **fires once** |

- **A fade with no rise reads as a loading glitch.** A rise **past 24 px reads
  as a slide.** 14 px is the band, not a starting point to tune upward.
- The `-12%` margin fires the reveal when the reader is looking, not when the
  first pixel clears the fold.
- `data-sc-in` is what the engine watches. Without it nothing fires and the
  stagger children stay hidden.
- **Content that re-hides on the way back up is a defect, not an effect.**
- *"Larger, slower, or bouncier is never more premium; the restraint is the
  signal."*

**A flow section directly after a pinned act takes reduced padding.** The
pinned stage needs a full viewport to scroll off, and full `--sc-section`
padding on top of that delays the flow section's first content by another
screen. The harness will not call it dead scroll — correctly, the stage is
moving — and the reader still sees a near-empty screen. Cut the block padding
there and start the first reveal near `p = 0`.

## Rail settle on `pan` (§3)

Lateral travel alone reads as a slideshow on rails. **Give the rail's items a
staggered settle driven from `--sc-p`** and they read as a drawer being
pulled instead.

- **Exempt the first item** — a `pan` act needs its opening content already
  present.
- **Floor the opacity around 0.55**, so a not-yet-settled card reads as
  arriving rather than as failing to load.

Upstream gates the settle to `prefers-reduced-motion` — **utgår, F-011**.
The settle always runs. What *does* survive from
the same passage is the reachability requirement, which is not a motion
preference at all: a `pan` rail's transform **is** the navigation, so nothing
may zero it and park the act on its first screenful. Every item in a rail
stays reachable, and that is checked on the sheet, not assumed.

Two more, from the same section:

- **Card copy is read while cropped.** Items enter and leave through the
  viewport edges, so a heading is half-shown for most of its life, and two
  half-headings side by side can read as a third word (`TRACE` beside
  `EVALUATE` becoming `RE EVALUATE`). Keep card headings to one or two short
  words and expect every line to be read partially cut off.
- If three items do not reach half a viewport of overflow, **the fix is more
  rail, not wider cards**: put the act's heading in as the first item and a
  closing note as the last. Both earn their place, and they add the width the
  travel needs.

## Devices that cannot share an element (§9)

**`magnet`, `parallax` and `cue` all write `transform`.** The magnet writes
every frame in its own rAF loop, so it silently wins and the cue's entrance
rise is discarded — a visible animation lost to a race, with nothing in the
console.

- On a magnetic CTA, set **`data-sc-rise="0"`** so the cue writes a no-op
  instead of losing to the magnet.
- A cued element that wants its own continuous transform drives an **inner
  wrapper** from `--sc-p` in CSS, rather than stacking a second device on the
  same node.

All three pointer devices **interpolate toward** the pointer rather than
tracking it directly: *"direct tracking reads as artificial because it carries
no momentum."* They stay gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so
touch never fires a false hover — that gate is a pointer-capability query, not
a motion preference, and it stands.
The reduced-motion half of the same sentence does not port (F-011).

## Kinetic type: the mask and the re-split (§5)

Each unit slides up from **behind a mask**, so it enters from a clean edge
rather than simply fading.

- **Line masks must reserve room for descenders.** A mask clipped to the line
  box shears the tails off g, y, p and j, *"and that is the single most common
  way this effect looks broken."*
- **Line splitting measures real line boxes, so it re-runs after
  `document.fonts.ready`.** Do not call it on text still loading its face. The
  same `fonts.ready` handle earns its place twice over: a webfont swapping in
  changes the measured height of every copy block, so anything sized against
  those blocks (a scrim plate, a rail) is wrong until it re-measures.
- Lines are almost always right; words for a short punch line; characters
  approximately never, *"because it turns reading into waiting."*
- **One kinetic headline per act, at most.**

## What makes a `count` land (§7)

- **Ease out, hard.** A cubic ease-out, so most of the distance goes by in the
  first third and the last digits settle slowly. *"A linear count reads as a
  slot machine."*
- **1.2–1.8 s.** Under a second and the reader misses that it moved; past two
  and they are waiting for a number they have already guessed.
- **Fires at half visibility, once**, so the reader is looking at it when it
  starts, and it never re-runs on the way back up.
- **Pair it with the fade.** A counter inside a `data-sc-in` stack rises in
  with its label and starts ticking as it arrives — *"the same numbers static
  on the page read as a spreadsheet."*
- Write the target exactly as it should render, commas included; the engine
  strips them before parsing and applies `tabular-nums` so the layout does not
  jitter.

**A concept, fictional or pre-launch brand has no verified figures, so it has
no counters.** The device suits a SaaS or agency page and will look good in
the score table, *"which is exactly the trap: every number you could put in it
would be invented."* Decide this before designing an act around a number, not
after. Real brand, real stats, or a different device.

## Appendix: pattern vocabulary

Named patterns from taste-skill § 10, carried here so orchestrator, builder
and reviewer name the same thing. It is a **vocabulary, not a menu** — several
entries below are banned as directions elsewhere in the chain (glassmorphism,
holographic foil, carousels, gooey menus) and appear here only so a critique
can say which trope it is refusing.

- **Hero** — Asymmetric Split · Editorial Manifesto · Video/Media Mask ·
  Kinetic-Type · Curtain-Reveal · Scroll-Pinned.
- **Nav** — Dock Magnification · Magnetic Button (`data-sc-magnet`) · Gooey
  Menu · Dynamic Island · Contextual Radial · Floating Speed Dial · Mega Menu
  Reveal.
- **Layout** — Bento Grid · Masonry · Chroma Grid · Split-Screen Scroll ·
  Sticky-Stack Sections.
- **Cards** — Parallax Tilt Card (`data-sc-tilt`) · Spotlight Border Card
  (`data-sc-spotlight`) · Glassmorphism Panel · Holographic Foil ·
  Tinder Swipe Stack · Morphing Modal.
- **Scroll** — Sticky Scroll Stack · Horizontal Scroll Hijack (= `pan`) ·
  Locomotive / Sequence Scroll (= `scrub`) · Zoom Parallax · Scroll Progress
  Path · Liquid Swipe Transition.
- **Galleries** — Dome Gallery · Coverflow Carousel · Drag-to-Pan Grid ·
  Accordion Image Slider · Hover Image Trail · Glitch Effect Image.
- **Type** — Kinetic Marquee · **Text Mask Reveal** (massive type as a
  transparent window onto video — this is K2's letter-window) · Text Scramble
  · Circular Text Path · Gradient Stroke Animation · Kinetic Typography Grid.
- **Micro** — Particle Explosion Button · Liquid Pull-to-Refresh · Skeleton
  Shimmer · Directional Hover-Aware Button · Ripple Click · Animated SVG Line
  Drawing · Mesh Gradient Background · Lens Blur Depth.

Names alone are not permission. A pattern still has to clear the fingerprint
gate, the register, and `../motion.md` before it ships.

## Never restyle the engine's classes (AB06, 2026-09-03)

Theme the engine only through its six colour tokens and two fonts. A project rule on
`.sc-stage`, `.sc-copy`, `.sc-scrim` or any other `.sc-*` class silently wins over the
engine: the console then says `[scrollcraft] act "…" will not pin: its stage computes
position:relative` and every pinned act scrolls away, leaving its spacer as dead scroll.
Read the console for `[scrollcraft]` warnings before anything else in Step 5, and run
`scripts/scroll_verify.py` — a blind one-shot cannot see either. The engine is opt-in per
grammar (scrub, pin, pan); a page that keeps the chain's own single set-piece + shared
reveal does not need it.
