asset, and it is what a QA pass compares the delivered frame against.
*"Generated assets must be placed into the implementation before handoff or documented as
blocked"* — never quietly downgraded to a gradient. That downgrade is the media-role drift
this file's next section already bans, caught one step earlier.

---

## Anti-averaging

Choose a dominant direction. Secondary references contribute narrow, named details;
they do not get to soften the primary one. The failure mode is specific: a dark
workbench reference, an acid-yellow document site, and a serif editorial page do not
average into a warm cream canvas with muted clay accents — **dark + acid + serif is
not cream + orange + polite serif.** Dark → cream, saturated → muted clay, sharp →
rounded, distinctive layout → generic hero-and-sections: each swap is the
intersection eating the direction, not synthesis.

Run these against the lock before shipping — ported from `anti-ai-slop.md`:

- **Identity test.** If the first viewport could belong to any other company,
  branding lost to averaging. Add the one detail that makes this unmistakably *this*
  brand's build.
- **Editorial test.** If swapping the logo for a coffee shop, boutique hotel, or
  literary magazine still makes the hero feel plausible, the build has drifted into
  generic calm-editorial slop regardless of what the lock says on paper.
- **Screenshot test.** Would this pass next to real products in the named
  register, or does it read as the safe middle every other page also landed on?

A lock that names a dominant primary and still fails these three was averaged during
implementation, not during research — check the built page against the lock's
"Reject" line specifically.

## Token-role and media-role preservation

**Token-role preservation.** A source's role for a colour, radius, shadow, or
component is part of the token, not separable from it. A CTA-only accent used as a
section background, a code-only syntax colour promoted to UI chrome, or a decorative
gradient turned into a core surface are all role drift. Preserve the role or drop
the token — never repurpose it to make a layout "work."

**Media-role preservation.** An image-led reference never collapses to text-only
because the image was hard to produce. If the real asset genuinely is not
available, the placeholder must be honest, not silent:

```text
Placeholder — [slot name]
Aspect: [ratio, e.g. 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile]
Art direction: [subject, lighting, crop the real asset will match]
Alt: [describes the intended real subject, not "placeholder image"]
```

A placeholder with no aspect ratio, no art direction, and generic alt text is the
same failure as no image at all — it just fails one render cycle later.

---

## Three persona sketches

`SKILL.md` Step 5 pass 12 and [`verbs/review.md`](verbs/review.md) § 4 both resolve ties
with "named personas". Nothing in the chain created any, so the tie-break pointed at an
artifact that did not exist. It does now, and it is three lines in `BRIEF.md` — not the
per-project persona documents upstream files away, which is a research deliverable this
chain has no room for.

Select and write **three**, following upstream's proportions (*"2–3 primary users, 1–2 edge
case users, 1 stress case user"*), compressed to one line each:

```text
Primary: [who they are] · [device and connection] · [what they came to do]
Edge:    [who sits at the margin] · [the ability or context that puts them there] · [what breaks first]
Stress:  [the same job under a named difficult circumstance] · [what they cannot afford to lose]
```

**The conditions are situational, not only permanent.** Upstream's spectrum is explicit that
*"bright sunlight, noisy environment, one hand occupied, driving, multitasking, emotional
distress, unfamiliar language, slow connection"* belong beside vision, hearing, motor and
cognitive conditions. A stress persona on a Swedish harbour-restaurant page is a person on a
phone, outdoors, in sun, deciding where to eat in the next ten minutes — and that persona
decides more layout questions than any abstract one.

**Write the intersections down.** *"A sighted user in bright sunlight has similar needs to a
low-vision user. A stressed parent holding a baby has similar motor constraints to someone
with limited hand mobility. A non-native speaker has similar needs to someone with a
cognitive processing difference."* Each intersection is a universal-design opportunity: one
fix that pays twice.

**Then ask the one question that makes the set honest:** *"Which persona makes you most
uncomfortable?"* — *"that one probably needs the most attention."* Ask it of the brief, and
of the user when there is a user to ask. Discomfort is the signal that a persona was
included for completeness and is about to be designed around rather than for.

Sketches that read as cardboard cutouts have failed. The check is upstream's own: *"do these
feel like real people, or cardboard cutouts?"*

## Feeding Step 2 and Step 5

**Into Step 2.** At **Tier 2**, the lock *is* the direction — its primary reference
sets the token commitments directly. At **Tiers 0–1**, the lock is the **quality
bar** the locked or derived system has to clear: the locked tokens still win on
value, but the captured references are what "as good as" means, concretely.

**Into Step 5 visual QA.** Carry the lock's fields straight into the QA pass:

```text
Source truth: [the reference lock, or the DESIGN.md it fed]
Implementation evidence: [local screenshot, deployed URL screenshot, captured app state]
Viewport/state: [desktop/mobile, route, theme, interaction state]
```

Classify findings P0–P3 (broken/unreadable · major drift from the lock · moderate
mismatch or missing state · post-handoff polish). **No handoff with an open P0, P1,
or P2.** A P3 may ship with the finding named; P0–P2 block.

## Worked example — Skärgårdskrogen (Swedish harbour restaurant, warm photographic)

A harbourside restaurant on the Bohuslän coast. Register: **warm photographic**
(`SKILL.md` register table — harbour restaurant, guesthouse, tourism, family
business), with `klova/` as this skill's own in-repo worked example for the
register (`house-physics.md`).

**Research loop:**

1. Broad aesthetic — "warm coastal Nordic hospitality."
2. Domain/category — harbourside seafood dining, Bohuslän archipelago.
3. Known brand — a west-coast Swedish harbour restaurant with a photograph-led site.
4. Register — warm photographic, per the table above; cross-check against `klova/`.
5. Anti-reference — the editorial-print register (`calyx.html`): its apparatus on a
   family harbour restaurant reads as pretension, not craft.

Four captured and read: `klova/` itself, two competitor harbour-restaurant sites,
and `calyx.html` as the anti-reference boundary check.

**Reference-lock block:**

```text
Primary reference/direction: klova/ — centred logo lockup over full-bleed harbour photography, no rail, no kicker, no edition marker.
Preserve: centred logo lockup with no rail; full-bleed hero photograph with generous framing air on secondary images; one real outlined button sized to be pressed; warm serif display at conversational (not oversized-drop-cap) scale; dark-navy footer as the page's one tonal inversion.
Borrow only: dotted carousel indicator for the food gallery (competitor B — klova/ has no gallery, so this is a genuinely new need, not a style import); 12px rounded image corners (competitor B).
Role rules: the outlined button is CTA-only, never a secondary link style; the navy footer tone is inversion-only, never a section background elsewhere on the page.
Media strategy: photo:unsplash, sourced and vendored per photo-sources.md until real restaurant photography is supplied; hero 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile, framed with 24-48px air — never full-bleed-with-type-over, the editorial-print move this build explicitly rejects.
Reject: kicker microformat, grain film, ledger pricing, edition markers, italic serif drop caps — all editorial-print apparatus a family harbour restaurant cannot plausibly publish.
Token commitments: warm ivory canvas; near-black ink; one terracotta accent used only on the button and one wordmark word (never as fill); slate captions with a separate, measured value for the dark footer ground.
```

**Decision ledger:**

| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm photographic, not editorial print | `SKILL.md` register table + anti-reference read of `calyx.html` | register selects apparatus | Family-run harbour restaurant, not a publishing entity |
| Centred logo lockup, no rail | `klova/` (primary) | layout role: identity-first hero | The photograph is the primary hire, not editorial structure |
| Real outlined button | `klova/` (primary) | CTA-only | Warm-photographic register expects a pressable button, unlike print/cinematic typeset links |
| Dotted carousel for gallery | Competitor B (borrowed) | gallery navigation only | `klova/` had no gallery; licensed as one named borrowed detail, not a wholesale style import |
| One terracotta accent, display-scale only | `house-physics.md` structural rule | accent role: CTA + display, never fill | Prevents the accent diluting into a second colour system |

A rejected direction here would average `klova/`'s warm photographic register with
`calyx.html`'s editorial apparatus into a soft-cream page with a restrained kicker
and a half-outlined button that is neither a typeset link nor a real one — the
dark+acid+serif-vs-cream+orange+polite-serif failure, in miniature.

## Two additions from the 2026-09-03 A/B run (AB05)

- **A colour-swapped word in a headline is a gate-89 signal even without a serif.** "Se *exakt* vad som ändrades" with *exakt* in the accent is the same reflex as the italic word swap; use it only when a locked reference does it and the word carries the claim.
- **Token commitments name the anatomy of every priced or listed surface.** Write `pricing: ledger (hairline rows, display numerals)` or `features: label-rail`, so the lock carries house physics into Step 4 instead of falling back to bordered cards.

200	writing them down is the whole point."*
201	
202	After shipping, append the row and say what it shares with prior rows — the
203	shared columns are exactly what the *next* build has to avoid.

  pinned acts with dwell. Spending scroll on them spends the visitor's
  patience on the part they will not remember.
- **A continuous world is the exception to pacing variety.** All of the above
  is about a page of *acts*. A worldflight is one camera move, and *"a camera
  that changes speed between legs reads as broken rather than as
  expressive."* There, hold one pace and let the peak carry the shape by being
  the single long leg — [`pace.md`](pace.md).

The total-length budget stays **8–14 viewport-heights**. Pacing is how that
budget is spent, not permission to spend more: *"a page that needs 20 vh to
land its curve has too many acts, not too little room."*

## The fingerprint gate

Registry: `VAULT/wiki/projects/_index/design-fingerprints.md`, per-vault,
starting from whatever rows already exist — not repeating **yourself** across
builds, not a universal constraint. **Six dimensions**, recorded per row:

| # | Dimension | What it records |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Grammar | Which of `grammars.md`, or a named new one |
| 2 | Nav treatment | What the chrome is and what it's for |
| 3 | Hero device | What the first screen does |
| 4 | Act-sequence shape | Device order, act count, total viewport-heights |
| 5 | Close pattern | How the last screen behaves, what the CTA sits in |
| 6 | Signature move | The one bespoke interaction, in a phrase |

**The gate: a new build must differ from EVERY existing row on at least 4 of
the 6** — four against each row individually, not averaged across the table.
Dimension 6 is free (unique by definition), so the gate really asks for 3
more out of the remaining 5 against each row. If the plan fails, **change
the plan, not the log** — rewriting a row to fit is what makes it worthless.

**Row format** — one row per shipped build, all six dimensions plus a world
note and the path: `| Build | Grammar | Nav | Hero device | Act-sequence
shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |`

**Rows are append-only.** From upstream `templates/FINGERPRINTS.md`:

> *"A build that has been superseded stays in the table, because the space it
> occupies is still occupied."*

A replaced, retired or rejected build keeps its row. The registry does not
record what is live; it records what surface has already been taken, and a
surface stays taken whether or not the build that claimed it is still up.
Deleting a row silently frees a shape for reuse, which is the same failure as
editing one to make room — *"never edit a row to make room for it. If a
planned build fails, change the plan."*

**Fill every column.** A row with blanks cannot be scored 4-of-6 against, so
it weakens the gate for every build after it.

**Keep a "what is taken" list beside the table.** Add a bullet whenever a
build claims something a later build should avoid reusing: a grammar, a nav
treatment, a close pattern, a signature move, an act-count-and-length band.
*"The shared columns are what the next build inherits as a constraint, so
writing them down is the whole point."*

After shipping, append the row and say what it shares with prior rows — the
shared columns are exactly what the *next* build has to avoid.

253	  i det egna repot (repots demosajter är per definition "på riktigt", inte en
254	  ogaterad kundmapp). Nästa session som rör kedjan äger att välja och bevisa vald
255	  väg åt båda hållen (en icke-triggande redigering nekas fortfarande att passera
256	  ogranskad; en riktig routningsträff mot `sites/` armar).
257	- **F-011 orsakade ingendera.** Motordiffen mot uppström är fyra rader.
258	  `var reduce = false` slog **på** playhead-lerpen (faktor 1,0 → 0,18) och tog inte bort
259	  någon utjämning; `reduce` gatear tio ställen och alla är avstängningsgrenar.
260	  F-012:s tredje hypotes är därmed motbevisad mot källan.
261	- **Regel:** (1) **Bespoke rörelse läser `--sc-ps`, aldrig rå `--sc-p`**, när den driver
262	  något ögat ser förflytta sig (transform, object-position, clip-path, mask-position).
263	  Cue-opacitet får läsa `--sc-p`. `--sc-ps` publiceras av
264	  `skills/design/scripts/scroll/sc-smooth.js`, som kopieras in bredvid motorn (motorn
265	  redigeras aldrig) och registrerar egenskapen som `<number>` så CSS kan interpolera den.
266	  (2) **"Ser hackigt ut" är två fel, och båda ska mätas innan något ändras** — takt och
267	  bildtid. En sida kan hålla 60 fps och ändå stega, och den kan glida perfekt i värdet
268	  och ändå tappa bilder. `motion_probe.py` rapporterar båda, och en signaturakt är inte
269	  klar förrän `staircase = 0`, `max_step ≤ 3 %`, p95 ≤ 20 ms och noll frames över 33 ms.
270	  (3) `will-change` sätts bara medan något rör sig; shimen städar motorns klassbreda
271	  promoveringar i vila.
272	- **Efterspel, 2026-09-08:** när `emil-design-eng` kördes över shimen (routern hade
273	  namngivit den och jag hade hoppat över den, alltså precis r7:s fel) föll tre buggar ut.
274	  Den allvarligaste: `--sc-ps` registrerades med `inherits: false`, vilket gör att ett
275	  **barn** som läser `var(--sc-ps)` får `0` i stället för förälderns värde. Akten hade
276	  stått fryst på varje sida som använde shimen, med ren konsol. Fixturen missade det
277	  eftersom den inlinade en miniatyr som aldrig registrerade egenskapen. Den laddar nu den
278	  riktiga filen. Två mindre: `will-change` sattes på akt-behållaren, som inte är elementet
279	  som rör sig, och värdet skrevs varje frame för varje akt, vilket kostar en
280	  subträds-omräkning för akter som står stilla. **Och `motion_probe` godkände buggen** —
281	  ett kort som aldrig rör sig är perfekt jämnt. Därför har proben nu en `DEAD`-kontroll:
282	  ett värde som inte rör sig alls medan sidan scrollas är ett fel, inte ett godkännande.
283	  Lärdomen är regeln, inte buggen: **en prob som kan godkänna en död sida är sämre än
284	  ingen prob**, och båda riktningarna måste bevisas mot samma fixtur.
285	- **Status:** `scripts/scroll/sc-smooth.js` (ny), `scripts/motion_probe.py` (ny),
286	  `tests/motion/{staircase,smooth}.html` (fixturer, bevisade i båda riktningarna),
287	  `tests/alunix-concepts-r5/motion-probe-v3b/` (mätningen sparad). F-012 är därmed
288	  stängd som fråga; V3b:s egen prestandaskuld är kvar och tas i V3c.
289	
290	## 2026-09-15 · r8-boarden (port 4626), K4 Delaren dömd som mönster, inte som sida
291	
292	### F-015 · Före/efter-delaren är ett referensmönster, inte ett helsideskoncept
293	- **Visades:** K4-r8 på boarden, hela sidan: den tippande delaren mellan
294	  `sites/before-ai-slop.html` och Calyx, R3-läget med plan 004 öppen.
295	- **Antons ord (ur beställningen 2026-09-15, återgivet):** K4-slidern från förra sessionen
296	  sparas som referens för den typen av före/efter-showcase, inte som helsideskoncept.
297	  Huvuduppgiften är i stället K3:s ritning som processakt i V3-sidan.
298	- **Dom:** hade kunnat bli bra som del, inte som helhet. Delaren som mekanik håller
299	  (två hela sidor i miniatyr, ps 0,40 med Calyx som vyns största objekt, verified i R3);
300	  som bärande idé för en hel byråsida räcker den inte.
301	- **Regel:** en showcase-mekanik som bevisar ett påstående (före/efter) är ett
302	  *mönster* i katalogen av egna akter, inte ett koncept. Den får återanvändas som en
303	  sektion i en sida vars grammatik bär den; den bygger ingen sida ensam. K4-cellen
304	  parkeras som det mönstret, med sin BRIEF, NOTES och `?preview=`-lägen som
305	  referensmaterial. Plan 004 (bildtexten klipps under 640) förblir öppen och stänger
306	  inte cellen, eftersom cellen inte längre ska skeppas.
307	- **Status:** bara här, plus raden i `tests/alunix-r8/STATUS.md` och `runs/K4/NOTES.md`.
308	
309	## 2026-09-19 · Antons stående förbud, ingen board — läst direkt av Alunix-sidan
310	
311	### F-016 · Liten "beskrivande" stiltypisk AI-text är helt förbjuden
312	- **Visades:** ingen board. Antons ord är ett stående beslut, inte en dom över en
313	  körning, men han pekade konkret på Alunix-sidan (`tests/alunix-r8`): små
314	  kickers/eyebrows ("EXEMPELCASE", "FRÅN EXEMPEL TILL ER SIDA", "SÅ GÅR DET TILL"),
315	  bildtexter ("Exempelsida: Hōrai, Asian fusion-koncept", "Exempelsida: Calyx, florist
316	  i Stockholm"), sidomenyer som listar stegrubriker i liten grå text, och små
317	  förklarande rader under rubriker i liten storlek ("Första steget är ett samtal om
318	  vad ni gör.").
319	- **Antons ord:** "All sån liten 'beskrivande' stiltypisk AI-text är härmed helt
320	  förbjuden och jag vill att designsystemet härmed aktivt arbetar emot det och kollar
321	  efter det i befintliga sidor."
322	- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt — inte begränsat till Alunix-cellen som visade det.
323	- **Regel:** ingen liten text vars enda jobb är att fylla, förklara det uppenbara,
324	  eller se designad ut. Testet: gör raden ett jobb läsaren behöver (identifierar,
325	  differentierar, lokaliserar eller möjliggör en handling), eller talar den bara om
326	  sidan/exemplet i mindre storlek än brödtexten? Det senare tas bort. Antons uttryckliga
327	  undantag: en sajts egen genre-apparat som är stilenlig OCH bär en funktion i den
328	  genren är inte utfyllnad — Calyx tidskriftsapparat (utgåva, löpnummer, plats-index)
329	  och Hōrais avsiktliga etiketter (rätt-namn, servis-nummer) identifierar verkliga
330	  saker på riktiga sajter i den genren; en digital byrås demo-sida i Alunix genre har
331	  ingen sådan licens.
332	- **Status:** portad till `anti-patterns.md` § Descriptive microtext (gate 99),
333	  `production-tells.md` gate 99, `gates.md`, SKILL.md § Apparatus (marknadssidor:
334	  default noll), kontroll `skills/design/scripts/microtext_scan.py`,
335	  `design-catalogue/MICROTEXT-AUDIT.md`.
336	
337	### F-017 · Prisliggarens displaystorlek är bara för siffror, inte för texten bredvid
338	- **Visades:** ingen board — samma session, prisliggarmönstret i katalogen
339	  (`house-physics.md` § Ledger, redan i bruk i Calyx/Hyperborea).
340	- **Antons ord (parafraserat i beställningen, samma dag):** displaystorlek i en
341	  priskolumn är bara för siffror (kompakta figurer som bildar rytm); text i samma
342	  kolumn ("Pris vid förfrågan") sätts ett steg mindre och linjeras mot siffrornas
343	  baslinje; en kontaktrad storleksätts som en handling, inte som en rubrik.
344	- **Dom:** regel, inte ett fel som redan visats — katalogens befintliga ledgers
345	  (Calyx, Hyperborea) skrevs redan så (siffra i display, valuta i kicker), men
346	  regeln stod inte skriven separat från valutaetiketten, så en textrad ("Pris vid
347	  förfrågan", "Kontakta oss") kunde av misstag ärva samma display-storlek som
348	  priset. Skrivs ner nu så nästa bygge inte chansar.
349	- **Regel:** i en ledger-rad bär enbart siffercellen display-storleken; en textcell i
350	  samma kolumn (`"Pris vid förfrågan"`, en enhet, en villkorstext) sätts ett
351	  typografiskt steg mindre än siffran och baslinjelinjeras mot den, aldrig
352	  samma storlek. En kontaktrad (telefon, mejl, boka-länk) storlekssätts som en
353	  handling — knapptext- eller länkstorlek — aldrig som en rubrik.
354	- **Status:** portad till `house-physics.md` § Ledger, never card grid, kontrollen
355	  `microtext_scan.py --price-ledger`.
356	
357	### F-018 · Sidan får aldrig berätta vad den strax ska göra
358	- **Visades:** boardgranskning 2026-09-20, Alunix V3d (`tests/alunix-r8`), ingressen
359	  under kapitelrubriken Exempelcase: "Calyx är en florist i Stockholm och Hōrai en
360	  restaurang. Ingen av dem finns, men sidorna är färdiga. Vi går igenom vad vi valde i
361	  dem och varför."
362	- **Antons ord:** "är återigen helt hjärndött, och precis samma AI-slop som jag
363	  reagerade på tidigare."
364	- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt. Samma familj som F-016, men en annan storlek: detta är
365	  brödtext, inte småtext, så `microtext_scan.py` ser den aldrig.
366	- **Diagnos, tre drag som bär felet:**
367	  1. **Färdplanen.** "Vi går igenom vad vi valde i dem och varför" beskriver sidans
368	     egen disposition. En läsare som ser en case-sektion vet redan att den innehåller
369	     case; raden talar om formen i stället för att säga något.
370	  2. **Brasklappen.** "Ingen av dem finns" ber om ursäkt för arbetet innan det visats,
371	     och sänker det läsaren just ska bedöma.
372	  3. **Uppställningen.** Formen uppställning → brasklapp → färdplan är LLM-default för
373	     "introducera ett avsnitt" och känns igen på sitt tempo, inte på sina ord.
374	- **Regel:** ingen text på sidan refererar till sidan. En ingress, en kicker eller en
375	  inledande rad handlar om verksamheten, arbetet eller läsarens fråga — aldrig om vad
376	  avsnittet nedanför innehåller, i vilken ordning det kommer, eller varför det finns.
377	  Ingen brasklapp om materialets status före materialet. Testet: stryk raden och se om
378	  läsaren tappar något annat än en beskrivning av det hen ändå ser. Gör hen inte det,
379	  var raden utfyllnad — och ett avsnitt som bara har en rubrik ska hellre sättas så att
380	  rubriken bär ensam än förses med en ingress som fyller ut.
381	- **Status:** portad till `anti-patterns.md` § Descriptive microtext (ny underrubrik
382	  § The page narrating itself), `production-tells.md` gate 99, `gates.md` gate 99,
383	  `skills/design/references/copy-gate.md`.
384	
385	## 2026-09-25 · r8-boarden (port 4626), V3g "Rutverket · mjuk showcase" runda 2
386	
387	### F-019 · Textrutans rubrik får inte ta över
388	- **Visades:** V3g R2, showcasens textruta på desktop med stegrubriken i cirka 120 px
389	  (`En mening som saktar in`, `Ett mejl räcker`) över ett stort skuggat stegtal (`03`, `05`).
390	- **Antons ord:** "showcasen är bättre men rubriken är alldeles för stor och ger inte önskad
391	  effekt, det tar över på ett dåligt sätt, testa en annan layout på texten men behåll
392	  mekanismen."
393	- **Dom:** mekanismen bra (övertoning, räknare, mintspår), typografin i rutan dålig.
394	- **Regel:** i en ruta som följer en levande sajt är sajten huvudsaken och texten
395	  bildtexten. Stegrubriken står i rubrikskala (h3, ungefär 28–32 px), inte i displayskala.
396	  Rutans tomma yta fylls med struktur (steglista, räknare), aldrig med förstorad text eller
397	  jättesiffror.
398	- **Status:** V3g EFFECTS.md, runda 3-briefen.
399	
400	### F-020 · Scrollen går för fort, och mjukheten får inte offras för farten
401	- **Visades:** V3g R2, hela sidan med Lenis-standard (ett hjulsteg = 100 px) och hero-pinnen
402	  `+=120%`.
403	- **Antons ord:** "när man scrollar ned en gång på hjulet så hoppar man ned från toppen av
404	  sidan och kastas förbi kortet så man knappt hinner se det vändas … tvinga sakta ned
405	  scrollen … var extra noga med att se till att den är mjuk och jämn hela vägen." Om
406	  showcasen: "den hoppar ned för sidan väldigt hastigt mellan texterna."
407	- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt.
408	- **Regel:** husets tempo är `wheelMultiplier: 0.6`, `lerp: 0.075`. En pin vars innehåll
409	  läsaren ska se ske spänner minst 200 vh. Den inbäddade sajten glider mellan ankare över
410	  större delen av segmentet, aldrig i ett ryck. Allt verifieras jämnt med `section_probe.py`.
411	- **Status:** `references/scroll/devices.md` § Load-bearing rules.
412	
413	### F-021 · En bra effekt försämrades av en ändring någon annanstans
414	- **Visades:** V3g R2 mot V3f. Tesrubriken "Det första intrycket är digitalt." var orörd i
415	  koden men märkbart mer statisk och ryckig.
416	- **Antons ord:** "var också bättre förra rundan, nu är den mer statisk och ryckig. Ta reda
417	  på anledningen … systemet får inte ta fel på bra effekter och göra de sämre, agenterna
418	  måste ha tydliga instruktioner och riktlinjer för vad som är bra."
419	- **Grundorsak (mätt):** iframes i en pinnad scen laddades om vid varje
420	  `ScrollTrigger.refresh()`, eftersom pin-spacern flyttar dem i DOM:en. Varje omladdning bad
421	  om en ny refresh, och loopen gick hela besöket: 6–12 omladdningar per iframe per pass.
422	  Felet fanns redan i V3f. R2 förladdade den andra sajten och dubblade kostnaden, och tesens
423	  p95 gick från 33 till 50–100 ms.
424	- **Regel:** godkända effekter skyddas. De står i körningens `EFFECTS.md` med en uppmätt
425	  signatur. Varje runda kör `section_probe.py` på HELA sidan mot baslinjen, och en sektion
426	  som blivit sämre blockerar rundan även om ingen rad i den ändrats. En iframe i en pin
427	  kräver en egen `pinSpacer`, och en refresh anropas aldrig från en iframes `load`.
428	- **Status:** `references/motion.md` § Approved effects are protected,
429	  `references/scroll/devices.md`, `scripts/section_probe.py`.

# FEEDBACK.md — Antons domar, en regel per post

Läses **alltid** i `design/SKILL.md` Step 1b, tillsammans med `TASTE.md`, innan Step 2.
Referensgolvet i `hooks/design-gate.py` spärrar första UI-skrivningen i ett nybygge tills
den här filen är läst. TASTE.md säger hur typ, bild, yta och rörelse ska samspela;
den här filen säger vad Anton faktiskt sagt om det kedjan byggt, och vilken regel som
följer av det.

**Så skrivs en post.** En dom = en post, samma session som domen. Fält: datum · runda/board ·
vad som visades · Antons ord (citat, oredigerat) · dom (bra / dåligt / hade kunnat bli bra om)
· regeln som härleds · status (var regeln portats: TASTE.md §, house-physics, SKILL.md,
eller "bara här"). Regel för orkestreraren: ingen board utan post innan `/conclude`.
Ta aldrig bort en post; en regel som visar sig fel får en ny post som upphäver den.

---

## 2026-09-06 · r6-boarden (port 4624), sex Alunix-celler, K1 Skymning / K2 Affischen / K3 Konsolen

### F-001 · Reservläget utan resa är tomt
- **Visades:** alla sex celler under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (Antons Windows har
  animationseffekter av).
- **Antons ord:** "det var ingen scroll effekt överhuvudtaget, eller någon annanstans. Inte
  heller på de andra sidorna. I övrigt var båda sidorna väldigt platta och intetsägande"
- **Dom:** dåligt. Rörelsen fanns i rörelseläget, men reservläget bar inte sekvensen, så
  sidan blev ett statiskt slutläge.
- **Regel:** under reduced motion visas set-piecets *formade* lägen i ordning som egna
  sektioner (samma lägen som `?preview=`), aldrig en tumnagel av målet och aldrig ett hopp
  till sista rutan. Orkestreraren granskar båda lägena som pixlar och anger läget per bild.
- **Status:** portad till SKILL.md § Motion, house-physics Motion, `design-stop.py` exit-bar
  (kräver rm-bild vid scroll), boardens varningsrad.

### F-002 · Målet i vila får inte förhandsvisa slutläget
- **Visades:** K1 körning 1 (kedjan): fönstret tänt med Hōrai-skärmbilden redan i stillhet.
  K1 körning 2 (native): fönstret tänds först vid scroll.
- **Antons ord:** "Det lilla fönstret i första scenen laddades statiskt från början i ena
  versionen och inte alls i den andra"
- **Dom:** dåligt (körning 1); körning 2:s lösning i rörelseläge är rätt.
- **Regel:** set-piecets mål (fönstret, ordet, objektet) är tyst i vila och tänds vid första
  scrollen; under reduced motion är det fullt närvarande som egen scen.
- **Status:** portad till house-physics Motion, SKILL.md § Motion, målbild K1 v2.

### F-003 · En auktoritet per sida, också när typen bär
- **Visades:** K2 båda körningarna: affischtyp 300 px+, stora skärmbilder och siffror i
  ordmärkesgrad på samma sida.
- **Antons ord:** "det blev 'för mycket', det balanserades inte ut någonstans utan blev bara
  jobbigt att kolla på, i båda versionerna"
- **Dom:** dåligt. Målbilden (Claudes) bad om två auktoriteter.
- **Regel:** ett displayelement per skärm; när typen bär är siffror kickers och skärmbilder
  plates i spalt. Orkestrerarens målbild måste namnge auktoriteten och vad som viker
  (målbildsgrinden, skill-orchestration § 12).
- **Status:** TASTE.md § 1 (redan), skill-orchestration § 12, målbild K2 v2.

### F-004 · Heron behöver något bredvid ordmärket
- **Visades:** K2 båda körningarna utan hero-bild; körning 2 (native) hade fotot *i*
  bokstäverna.
- **Antons ord:** "Båda saknade även hero-bild och lånade bara element från Calyx, körning
  2:s version med bild under texten hade kunnat bli väldigt bra med något mer i hero:n,
  kanske en bild bredvid eller en neutral bakgrund"
- **Dom:** hade kunnat bli bra om. Bokstavsfönstren är rätt idé.
- **Regel:** en typburen hero får en enda dämpad plate bredvid ordmärket (svartvitt,
  dokumentärt), aldrig under; fönstren i bokstäverna ska visa exempelsajterna, inte
  Calyx-fotot ensamt. Antons val 2026-09-06: platen bredvid.
- **Status:** målbild K2 v2; bara här.

### F-005 · Typsnittsblandningen i K2 körning 1 är förebild
- **Visades:** K2 körning 1 (kedjan): två snitt med tydliga roller.
- **Antons ord:** "körning 1 gjorde typografin betydligt intressantare med en bättre
  blandning av typsnitt"
- **Dom:** bra.
- **Regel:** två snitt, rollerna korsar aldrig (TASTE.md § 4.2); K2 v2 utgår från r6
  B-K2:s val.
- **Status:** målbild K2 v2; bara här.

### F-006 · Glaskort med telemetri över ett foto är AI-slop
- **Visades:** K3 båda körningarna.
- **Antons ord:** "'Konsolerna' var katastrofal AI- slop, jag vet inte ens vad det skulle
  likna för något."
- **Dom:** dåligt. Felet satt i målbilden (Claudes), inte i byggarna.
- **Regel:** glaskort, dashboard-över-foto, "live"-punkter och telemetri-chrome hör till
  AI-troplistan och stoppas i målbildsgrinden innan någon brief skrivs.
- **Status:** skill-orchestration § 12 (troplistan), TASTE.md § 5 (komplement).

### F-007 · Matchar inte målbilden = blockerande fel
- **Visades:** K1 båda körningarna mot målbildens "kameran åker in i ett fönster".
- **Antons ord:** "Outputen i den första scenen matchade inte alls beskrivningen i planen."
- **Dom:** dåligt.
- **Regel:** orkestreraren jämför signaturakten mot målbilden bild för bild i rörelseläge
  innan någon annan granskning; avvikelse från signaturakten stoppar rundan.
- **Status:** skill-orchestration § 12 (runda 2); bara här.

### F-008 · Referenserna måste läsas, och briefen får inte förbjuda dem
- **Visades:** noll lästa filer under `design/references/`, ingen TASTE.md, i alla
  kedjeceller.
- **Antons ord:** "skillkedjan inte verkade fyrade som den skulle, med noll referenser
  kollade över alla körningar, vilket är grunden till att den ska fungera"
- **Dom:** dåligt (kedjan och orkestrerarens prompt).
- **Regel:** TASTE.md + FEEDBACK.md + reference-lock + katalogposternas filer inkl.
  `extract/*-DESIGN.md` läses alltid; vid scrollbrief även `scroll/devices.md` +
  `feel-and-fingerprint.md`; hooken nekar annars första UI-skrivningen.
- **Status:** SKILL.md Step 1b/2b, `design-gate.py` referensgolv, `design-vision-track.py`
  `ref-read`, skill-orchestration § 12.

### F-009 · Modellstorlek syns inte i one-shot-läge
- **Visades:** sju Fable-high-processer med samma prompt, ingen dialog.
- **Antons ord:** "jag märker faktiskt ingen skillnad på kvaliteten på Fable-agenternas
  output jämfört med Sonnet"
- **Dom:** iakttagelse, inte en regel om modellen. Formatet (spec som implementation, en
  runda, varv brända på infrastruktur) neutraliserar modellen.
- **Regel:** delegerade byggen körs i rundor med fold-grind och pixelläsning emellan;
  infrastruktur (server, foton, genererat material) levereras av orkestreraren.
- **Status:** skill-orchestration § 12, `scripts/serve.py`, r7-harnesset.

### F-010 · Hōrai är ett fönster i fasaden, inte en ruta utanpå den
- **Visades:** r6 K1 (kedjan) i rörelseläge, `tests/alunix-ab-r6/review/B-K1/grid-motion.png`
  20–25 %: Hōrai-skärmbilden ligger som en platt rektangel ovanpå fasaden medan fotot zoomas.
- **Antons ord:** "Se till att Horai-rutan INTE ligger statisk utanpå fasaden som nu, utan
  visas som ett fönster i fasaden först när man kommer närmare, för att sedan zoomas in, se
  även till att övergången FRÅN horai görs dynamiskt och snyggt"

  läsaren ska se ske spänner minst 200 vh. Den inbäddade sajten glider mellan ankare över
  större delen av segmentet, aldrig i ett ryck. Allt verifieras jämnt med `section_probe.py`.
- **Status:** `references/scroll/devices.md` § Load-bearing rules.

### F-021 · En bra effekt försämrades av en ändring någon annanstans
- **Visades:** V3g R2 mot V3f. Tesrubriken "Det första intrycket är digitalt." var orörd i
  koden men märkbart mer statisk och ryckig.
- **Antons ord:** "var också bättre förra rundan, nu är den mer statisk och ryckig. Ta reda
  på anledningen … systemet får inte ta fel på bra effekter och göra de sämre, agenterna
  måste ha tydliga instruktioner och riktlinjer för vad som är bra."
- **Grundorsak (mätt):** iframes i en pinnad scen laddades om vid varje
  `ScrollTrigger.refresh()`, eftersom pin-spacern flyttar dem i DOM:en. Varje omladdning bad
  om en ny refresh, och loopen gick hela besöket: 6–12 omladdningar per iframe per pass.
  Felet fanns redan i V3f. R2 förladdade den andra sajten och dubblade kostnaden, och tesens
  p95 gick från 33 till 50–100 ms.
- **Regel:** godkända effekter skyddas. De står i körningens `EFFECTS.md` med en uppmätt
  signatur. Varje runda kör `section_probe.py` på HELA sidan mot baslinjen, och en sektion
  som blivit sämre blockerar rundan även om ingen rad i den ändrats. En iframe i en pin
  kräver en egen `pinSpacer`, och en refresh anropas aldrig från en iframes `load`.
- **Status:** `references/motion.md` § Approved effects are protected,
  `references/scroll/devices.md`, `scripts/section_probe.py`.

1	---
2	title: "Deon Libra"
3	url: https://deonlibra.com
4	source_url: https://deonlibra.com
5	captured: 2026-09-04
6	origin: raw-url
7	extract: ok
8	category: consumer-brand
9	category2: playful
10	family: marquee-condensed-attitude
11	dna: "Drop-culture DTC wellness x scrolling marquee protest copy"
12	register: cinematic dark
13	grammar: rhythmic cutlist
14	lane: "A cinematic hero photo sits between two scrolling marquee tickers, then black product-grid panels alternate with cream press/awards bands and a dark-red archival-photo statement section"
15	mode: persuade
16	traits: ["scrolling marquee ticker text (top and bottom)", "condensed bold display sans (Anton)", "black ground with red accent", "cream product-card panels", "press-logo wall", "archival family photography", "email signup modal", "accessibility widget button"]
17	palette: ["#000000", "#FFF8E7", "#C00121", "#887871", "#212018", "#E2DACC", "#703D2E", "#A99E93"]
18	type: ["Anton", "Inter"]
19	measured: designlang (confirmed)
20	kind: reference-style
21	source: claude
22	status: ready
23	raw: raw/e7889ca27eaac05c-deonlibra-com.webp
24	---
25	
26	## Why it works
27	
28	The page opens between two moving marquee tickers — a thin cream strip above
29	the nav ("THE SCENT OF EXPENSIVE HOBBIES IS HERE") and a bold red strip below
30	the hero ("THIS IS NOT A BEAUTY BRAND") — so the brand's attitude is stated in
31	motion before any product is shown. The hero photograph itself (a clay tennis
32	court, balls mid-bounce) has nothing to do with the product literally; it's
33	establishing a lifestyle register — leisure, expense, ritual — that the
34	condensed all-caps headline ("WELLNESS ROOTED IN RITUAL, ART, AND DROP
35	CULTURE") then names directly.
36	
37	One display face, Anton — extremely condensed, extremely bold — carries every
38	headline, ticker and section statement at consistent weight, so scale is the
39	only variable used for emphasis; nothing shifts in style, only in size. Body
40	copy and product data drop to a plain Inter, keeping the loud parts loud and
41	the informational parts quiet. Product cards run on a black ground with cream
42	frames, a red "on sale" flag, and product photography with visible packaging
43	copy (the products themselves are typeset like the site, condensed bold
44	labels) — so the packaging and the page share one visual system rather than
45	photography being the only brand touchpoint.
46	
47	The "Our Why" section breaks from product entirely into a dark maroon panel
48	with archival-style photography and a direct, culturally specific statement
49	("EVEN WHILE SLEEPING, BLACK PEOPLE CANNOT REST") — copy doing real narrative
50	work rather than generic brand-voice copy, which is unusual enough in this
51	genre to be the site's strongest asset.
52	
53	## What to borrow (principle)
54	
55	- **Use scrolling marquee tickers as attitude statements**, not just
56	  promotional banners — putting the brand's point of view in constant motion
57	  makes it unmissable without a large static block.
58	- **Choose hero photography for register, not for product literalism** — a
59	  tennis court says "expensive leisure" faster than a product shot would.
60	- **Run one extremely condensed, extremely bold display face at every scale**
61	  so hierarchy comes entirely from size, keeping the whole page visually
62	  coherent even across very different section types.
63	- **Let real, specific, culturally-grounded copy carry a "why" section** —
64	  it reads as conviction, not as brand-voice filler.
65	- **Match product packaging typography to the site's own type system** so
66	  photography and page feel like one continuous brand object.
67	
68	## What to leave
69	
70	- The email-signup modal fires early and covers most of the hero on load —
71	  worth testing timing/frequency against how much of the marquee/hero attitude
72	  gets seen before it's obscured.
73	- Two marquee tickers running simultaneously (top and bottom of hero) plus a
74	  third mid-page risks becoming visual noise rather than emphasis if overused
75	  further down the page.
76	- Extremely condensed display type at small sizes (as seen in some award/press
77	  captions) pushes legibility — fine at headline scale, marginal at caption
78	  scale.
79	
80	## Signature move
81	
82	Twin scrolling marquee tickers bracketing the hero — one understated
83	(top nav strip), one loud and red ("THIS IS NOT A BEAUTY BRAND") — stating the
84	brand's point of view in constant motion before any product appears.
85	
86	## Motion
87	
88	(from designlang extract) The extract rates overall feel "responsive" with
89	confirmed scroll-linked behaviour. Five duration steps span 100ms to 800ms,
90	mostly on a snappy custom ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.3, 1, 0.3, 1)`, 107
91	uses — the dominant curve on the page) with three more measured custom curves
92	(30 uses combined) for slower transitions. Four keyframes are confirmed
93	in use: `scrolling-left` (transform + visibility, 22 uses) is the mechanism
94	behind the marquee tickers; `rotator` and `dash` (7 uses each) drive a
95	rotating/SVG-progress element; `junipNodeInserted` (1 use) is a third-party
96	review-widget (Junip) insertion animation, not brand motion. Additional
97	keyframes — `text-underlined` (a link-hover underline wipe), `zoom-fade` /
98	`zoom-fade-short` (scale 1.1-1.2→1 with fade), and `spin` — are defined in the
99	stylesheet but not registered as in-use at scan time. (observed in capture)
100	The marquee ticker text is a continuous horizontal scroll/loop, confirmed by

mode: persuade
traits: ["scrolling marquee ticker text (top and bottom)", "condensed bold display sans (Anton)", "black ground with red accent", "cream product-card panels", "press-logo wall", "archival family photography", "email signup modal", "accessibility widget button"]
palette: ["#000000", "#FFF8E7", "#C00121", "#887871", "#212018", "#E2DACC", "#703D2E", "#A99E93"]

measured: designlang (confirmed)

## Why it works

The page opens between two moving marquee tickers — a thin cream strip above
the nav ("THE SCENT OF EXPENSIVE HOBBIES IS HERE") and a bold red strip below
the hero ("THIS IS NOT A BEAUTY BRAND") — so the brand's attitude is stated in
motion before any product is shown. The hero photograph itself (a clay tennis
court, balls mid-bounce) has nothing to do with the product literally; it's
establishing a lifestyle register — leisure, expense, ritual — that the
condensed all-caps headline ("WELLNESS ROOTED IN RITUAL, ART, AND DROP
CULTURE") then names directly.

One display face, Anton — extremely condensed, extremely bold — carries every
headline, ticker and section statement at consistent weight, so scale is the
only variable used for emphasis; nothing shifts in style, only in size. Body
copy and product data drop to a plain Inter, keeping the loud parts loud and
the informational parts quiet. Product cards run on a black ground with cream
frames, a red "on sale" flag, and product photography with visible packaging
copy (the products themselves are typeset like the site, condensed bold
labels) — so the packaging and the page share one visual system rather than
photography being the only brand touchpoint.

The "Our Why" section breaks from product entirely into a dark maroon panel
with archival-style photography and a direct, culturally specific statement
("EVEN WHILE SLEEPING, BLACK PEOPLE CANNOT REST") — copy doing real narrative
work rather than generic brand-voice copy, which is unusual enough in this
genre to be the site's strongest asset.

## What to borrow (principle)

- **Use scrolling marquee tickers as attitude statements**, not just
  promotional banners — putting the brand's point of view in constant motion
  makes it unmissable without a large static block.
- **Choose hero photography for register, not for product literalism** — a
  tennis court says "expensive leisure" faster than a product shot would.
- **Run one extremely condensed, extremely bold display face at every scale**
  so hierarchy comes entirely from size, keeping the whole page visually
  coherent even across very different section types.
- **Let real, specific, culturally-grounded copy carry a "why" section** —
  it reads as conviction, not as brand-voice filler.
- **Match product packaging typography to the site's own type system** so
  photography and page feel like one continuous brand object.

## What to leave

- The email-signup modal fires early and covers most of the hero on load —
  worth testing timing/frequency against how much of the marquee/hero attitude
  gets seen before it's obscured.
- Two marquee tickers running simultaneously (top and bottom of hero) plus a
  third mid-page risks becoming visual noise rather than emphasis if overused
  further down the page.
- Extremely condensed display type at small sizes (as seen in some award/press
  captions) pushes legibility — fine at headline scale, marginal at caption
  scale.

## Signature move

Twin scrolling marquee tickers bracketing the hero — one understated
(top nav strip), one loud and red ("THIS IS NOT A BEAUTY BRAND") — stating the
brand's point of view in constant motion before any product appears.

## Motion

(from designlang extract) The extract rates overall feel "responsive" with
confirmed scroll-linked behaviour. Five duration steps span 100ms to 800ms,
mostly on a snappy custom ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.3, 1, 0.3, 1)`, 107
uses — the dominant curve on the page) with three more measured custom curves
(30 uses combined) for slower transitions. Four keyframes are confirmed
in use: `scrolling-left` (transform + visibility, 22 uses) is the mechanism
behind the marquee tickers; `rotator` and `dash` (7 uses each) drive a
rotating/SVG-progress element; `junipNodeInserted` (1 use) is a third-party
review-widget (Junip) insertion animation, not brand motion. Additional
keyframes — `text-underlined` (a link-hover underline wipe), `zoom-fade` /
`zoom-fade-short` (scale 1.1-1.2→1 with fade), and `spin` — are defined in the
stylesheet but not registered as in-use at scan time. (observed in capture)
The marquee ticker text is a continuous horizontal scroll/loop, confirmed by
the raw and fresh captures showing different text scroll positions on the
same strip. An email-signup modal appears over the hero within the first few
seconds of load (observed — present in the fresh capture, absent in the raw
one), suggesting a timed rather than scroll-triggered trigger.

|---|---|
| durations | xs 100ms · sm 200ms · md 300ms · lg 500ms · xl 800ms |
| easings | ease-out `cubic-bezier(0.3, 1, 0.3, 1)` (107×, dominant) · custom (30×) |
| keyframes in use | `scrolling-left` (marquee) · `rotator` · `dash` · `junipNodeInserted` (3rd-party) |

## Brief

Build a DTC lifestyle/wellness brand around one moving marquee ticker stating
the brand's attitude in a short, quotable line, bracketing a hero photograph
chosen for lifestyle register rather than literal product content. Run one
extremely condensed, extremely bold display face at every heading scale, with
a plain grotesque for body and product data. Alternate black product-grid
panels (cream card frames, one red accent for sale flags/CTAs) with cream
press-logo and awards bands. Include one section that breaks from product
entirely — a dark accent panel with archival-style photography and specific,
first-person copy stating why the brand exists, not generic mission language.
Match product packaging typography to the site's own display face so
photography reads as part of the same system.

## Image recipe

Documentary or archival-style photograph of [SUBJECT], warm desaturated
colour grading evoking film stock, candid or environmental framing rather than
studio product staging, chosen to establish a lifestyle or cultural register
connected to the brand rather than to depict the product literally.

## Photo search

Unsplash first, Pexels second.
- "clay tennis court balls documentary"
- "archival family photograph film grain"
- "vintage sports photography 90s"
- "product still life red black minimal"

## Reference lock

Primary reference/direction: Deon Libra — marquee-ticker attitude statements,
condensed bold display type at every scale, black/cream/red DTC system.
Preserve (3-5 traits): a scrolling marquee ticker stating brand attitude in a
short line, bracketing the hero; one extremely condensed bold display face
carrying every headline and ticker at consistent weight; black ground with
cream card frames and one red accent for CTAs/sale flags; hero photography
chosen for lifestyle register rather than literal product depiction; at least
one section with specific, first-person "why" copy over archival-style
photography.
Borrow only (1-2): the accessibility-widget floating button; the "-14%" red
sale flag on product cards.
Role rules: display face never drops below a legible caption size; red accent
reserved for CTAs, sale flags and the loudest ticker only, never a large
background fill.
Media strategy: photo:unsplash — documentary/archival-toned photography for
lifestyle and "why" sections; clean studio product photography only for
product-grid cards.
Reject: a second display typeface; generic mission-statement copy in place of
specific narrative; a static banner in place of the moving marquee.
Token commitments: ink `#000000`, cream `#FEF8E6`, red `#C10221`, maroon
`#703D2E`, stone `#887871`, stone-light `#A99E93`; display "Anton" (condensed
bold caps), body "Inter".

2	title: "TOMO"
3	url: https://tomoseattle.com/
4	source_url: https://tomoseattle.com/
5	captured: 2026-09-04
6	origin: refero
7	extract: ok
8	category: hospitality
9	category2: playful
10	family: zine-fridge-collage
11	dna: "Torn-paper sticker navigation x rubber-stamp tomato-red marquee"
12	register: illustrated dark
13	grammar: gallery/catalog
14	lane: "A warm linen page opens on a red marquee ribbon and a viewport-wide serif wordmark, then unfolds as an art-directed collage of overlapping food and street photography with torn-paper sticker labels — no card grid, no menu accordion, no reservation widget"
15	mode: experience
16	traits: ["120px wordmark, single line, no padding", "torn-paper sticker nav, not a bar", "one red, marquees and stamps only, never a button", "0px radius, 1px black hairline everywhere", "full-bleed collage, overlapping and rotated", "no max-width container on the homepage"]
17	palette: ["#eee2d4", "#000000", "#ffffff", "#ff6347", "#efefef"]
18	type: ["Recife", "Times"]
19	measured: designlang (confirmed)
20	kind: reference-style
21	source: anton
22	status: ready
23	refero: processed/TOMO.md
24	---
25	
26	## Why it works
27	
28	Palette and type are read from Refero's extracted tokens, confirmed by the
29	live capture. Warm linen `#eee2d4` is the sole canvas — the source states
30	white is a surface only, never the page background — and tomato red
31	`#ff6347` is fenced entirely to marquee ribbons and rubber-stamp text, with
32	an explicit ban on ever using it as a button fill. That restriction is what
33	keeps the one loud colour reading as printed ink (a stamp, a strip of taped
34	paper) rather than as UI chrome asking to be clicked.
35	
36	Recife carries the entire display voice at a single light weight (300),
37	scaled from the 96px section titles up to a ~120px wordmark that spans the
38	viewport with no padding — "the heaviest typographic moment on any page."
39	Times, kept deliberately small at 13px, exists only for functional fine
40	print, so the system never confuses "large and serif" with "small and
41	serif" — the two sit at opposite, non-overlapping ends of the scale with
42	nothing in between.
43	
44	The layout refuses every restaurant-website convention by name: no
45	accordion menus, no floating reservation widget, no colour-coded CTAs. Every
46	photograph sits at 0px radius with only a 1px black hairline (or nothing),
47	overlapping and bleeding off the frame like a collage taped to cream paper
48	rather than a card grid — and navigation itself becomes physical objects
49	(torn-paper stickers with borders) instead of a conventional nav bar.
50	
51	## What to borrow (principle)
52	
53	- **Fence the one accent colour to non-interactive surfaces only.** Banning
54	  red from ever being a button fill — reserving it for marquees and stamps —
55	  keeps a bold colour readable as ink, not as a call to action.
56	- **Turn navigation into physical objects, not a bar.** Rendering nav items
57	  as individual bordered "stickers" with gaps between them, rather than a
58	  unified nav container, reinforces the collage/zine metaphor structurally.
59	- **Refuse category-specific web conventions by name.** Explicitly ruling out
60	  accordion menus and floating reservation widgets forces genuinely different
61	  solutions instead of defaulting to industry templates.
62	- **Let photography overlap and bleed instead of gridding it.** Images placed
63	  at irregular scale and position, allowed to overlap type and each other,
64	  read as a collage rather than a card layout.
65	- **Keep a whisper-weight display serif at genuinely extreme scale.** Weight
66	  300 at 80-120px only works because the size itself carries the authority —
67	  adding weight would collapse the "elegant, not heavy" effect the source
68	  names directly.
69	
70	## What to leave
71	
72	- Zero max-width container on the homepage is a deliberate full-bleed choice
73	  that depends on carefully art-directed positioning at every breakpoint; a
74	  responsive rebuild without that same care will collapse into visual noise.
75	- Banning shadows, radius, and any elevation language entirely removes a
76	  common toolkit for signalling "this is clickable" — every interactive
77	  element instead needs a border or fill-change to read as actionable.
78	- A single-accent, no-CTA-button system genuinely limits conversion-focused
79	  design; a reservation flow or checkout would need to invent its own
80	  affordance language within these constraints.
81	
82	## Signature move
83	
84	The rubber-stamp section title: large display text (80-120px) rendered with
85	a distressed, slightly rotated offset-print texture, floating art-directed
86	(never centred) over a photography collage — treating a section header as a
87	printed stamp mark rather than a typeset heading.
88	
89	## Motion
90	
91	(from designlang extract) Feel reads as smooth, and the page is scroll-linked.
92	The system is genuinely minimal: one duration (200ms) on a plain `ease` curve.
93	Two keyframes are confirmed firing — `fade-pulse-in` (an opacity fade) and
94	`spin-loading` (a rotate transform) — the latter almost certainly a loading
95	spinner rather than brand choreography, consistent with the "surfaces never
96	lift... this is a printed page, not a glass UI" elevation philosophy holding
97	for everything except a functional loading state. (observed in capture) the
98	live capture confirms a static, collage-composed layout matching the
99	structure (marquee, wordmark, sticker nav, photo collage) with no visible
100	animated reveal beyond that; any interaction state most plausibly relies on a
101	border or fill swap on the sticker nav, on the same 200ms `ease`.
102	
103	| Token | Value | Easing |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| sm | 200ms | `ease` |
106	| fade-pulse-in | opacity fade | 1 use |
107	| spin-loading | rotate transform | loading spinner |
108	
109	## Brief
110	
111	Build a full-bleed, collage-style restaurant homepage with no max-width
112	container. Canvas is warm linen `#eee2d4` everywhere; white is a surface
113	colour only (sticker fills, reverse-type panels), never the background. Open
114	with a full-bleed tomato-red `#ff6347` marquee ribbon of uppercase Recife
115	text, then a single-line wordmark at up to 120px, weight 300, spanning the
116	viewport with no padding. Render navigation as individual white, 1px-
117	bordered "sticker" labels with small gaps between them, not a bar. Lay
118	photography as an art-directed collage — 0px radius, 1px black hairline
119	borders or none, images overlapping and bleeding off the frame at varying
120	scale, never in an equal-gutter grid. Float rubber-stamp section titles
121	(80-120px, rotated 2-4°, distressed texture) over the photo collage,
122	positioned asymmetrically. Reserve tomato red strictly for marquees and
123	stamp ink — never a button fill, never a CTA. Keep body/caption text small
124	(13-26px) and functional. Space sections with 65-115px padding; no shadows,
125	no gradients, no rounded corners anywhere.
126	
127	## Image recipe
128	
129	Tightly cropped documentary photograph of [SUBJECT] — food close-ups or
130	neighbourhood street scenes shot in natural light with saturated, unfiltered
131	colour, no soft-focus or styled food-photography lighting, cropped tight and
132	placed to overlap or bleed off the frame edge as a collage element rather
133	than a standalone hero image.
134	
135	## Photo search
136	
137	Unsplash first, Pexels second.
138	- "food close up natural light saturated"
139	- "neighborhood street photography documentary"
140	- "restaurant interior candid natural light"
141	- "vintage sign storefront street photography"
142	
143	## Reference lock
144	
145	Primary reference/direction: TOMO — zine-collage restaurant homepage, torn-
146	paper sticker nav, tomato-red marquees and stamps only.
147	Preserve (3-5 traits): warm linen `#eee2d4` as the sole background, white as
148	a surface colour only; tomato red `#ff6347` confined to marquee ribbons and
149	stamp text, never a button or CTA fill; Recife weight 300 for every display
150	moment (80-120px), Times reserved for 13px fine print only, nothing between;
151	0px radius and 1px black hairline as the only border language; full-bleed,
152	overlapping, asymmetric photo collage with no max-width container.
153	Borrow only (1-2): the rotated rubber-stamp section-title texture; the
154	torn-paper sticker nav-item treatment.
155	Role rules: red never fills a button or clickable chip; Times never sets
156	display text; the layout is never centred by default — composition is
157	always art-directed and asymmetric.
158	Media strategy: photo:unsplash — tightly cropped, saturated documentary food
159	and street photography; no soft-focus styling, no lifestyle staging.
160	Reject: any filled red CTA button; box-shadow or gradient anywhere; rounded
161	corners on any element; a centred/gridded card layout; a max-width container
162	on the homepage.
163	Token commitments: bg `#eee2d4`, ink `#000000`, surface `#ffffff`, accent
164	`#ff6347`, neutral `#efefef`; display Recife 300 at 80-120px/leading 1.0;
165	body 13-26px; radius 0px universal; base spacing unit 6px, section gap
166	65-115px.

1	---
2	title: "EXAMPLE"
3	url: https://www.weareexample.com
4	source_url: https://www.weareexample.com
5	captured: 2026-09-04
6	origin: raw-url
7	raw: raw/24ad4c5cd6218a7f-www-weareexample-com.webp
8	extract: ok
9	category: portfolio
10	category2: hospitality
11	family: condensed-marquee-agency
12	dna: "Culture-agency manifesto poster x hotel-lounge marquee reel"
13	register: modern clean
14	grammar: typographic poster
15	lane: "A giant condensed black headline wedges small client photos into its own letterforms, then a full-bleed hotel-lounge photo carries a horizontal scrolling marquee of the same copy"
16	mode: persuade
17	traits: ["off-white ground", "ultra-bold condensed display sans", "photos wedged into headline letterforms", "italic script sub-tagline", "horizontal marquee text over photo", "warm red-lit interior photography", "numbered slide counter", "minimal single-line nav"]
18	palette: ["#F3F3F3", "#7A4B2E", "#380907", "#0F141B", "#730909", "#907663"]
19	type: ["American Grotesk Compressed", "Ppeditorialnew"]
20	measured: designlang
21	kind: reference-style
22	source: claude
23	status: ready
24	---
25	
26	## Why it works
27	
28	The page opens with one device doing double duty: an oversized, ultra-bold condensed
29	headline ("AN EARNED-LED CULTURE AGENCY") that reads as pure typography from a distance,
30	but has two small client-work photographs wedged directly into its negative space, tucked
31	between letters at an angle. The headline is the hero image and the proof point at once —
32	there's no separate "our work" gallery competing for the same attention in the first
33	screen.
34	
35	Directly beneath it, a full-bleed, warm red-lit hotel-lounge photograph carries a second
36	typographic device: a horizontal marquee of oversized white type ("...AND HOTELS TRAVEL
37	...") scrolling across the image at a scale that partially exceeds the viewport, with a
38	small `02/03` counter centred at the top. Because both the headline and the marquee use
39	the same ultra-condensed, ultra-bold face, the page reads as one continuous typographic
40	voice even though the mechanism (static wedge vs. scrolling band) changes.
41	
42	An italic script line — "We Make It Happen" — sits alone in the quiet gap between the two
43	loud sections, functioning as the page's only soft, humanising mark against two very hard
44	typographic devices. The restraint of introducing a second type voice exactly once, at the
45	lowest-intensity moment, keeps it from diluting the condensed system.
46	
47	## What to borrow (principle)
48	
49	- **Wedge real work photography into the negative space of giant type**, rather than
50	  running a headline and a portfolio grid as separate zones — the credibility and the
51	  hook arrive in the same glance.
52	- **Reuse one condensed, ultra-bold voice across both a static headline and a moving
53	  marquee.** The mechanism can change (static vs. scrolling) as long as the type doesn't.
54	- **Save a second, softer typeface for exactly one low-intensity moment** — a tagline, a
55	  closing line — so it reads as a considered break, not a second system.
56	- **Let a full-bleed photo carry oversized type that exceeds the frame.** Type running off
57	  both edges signals scale and confidence without needing more copy.
58	
59	## What to leave

opacity for a blinking-indicator effect, `hr-marquee`/`demoLogoMarquee` loop a horizontal
translate to -50% for the scrolling logo wall, `hr-underline-sweep` wipes a link underline
out then back in across a hover, and the generic Tailwind `enter`/`exit` pair plus two
scale-pop keyframes (one with a fixed 45° rotate, one without) handle small icon/badge
pop-ins. No stagger or choreography pattern is documented beyond scroll-triggered section
entry (from designlang extract).

| token | value | used for |
|---|---|---|
| xs | 150ms | micro/hover transitions |
| sm | 200ms | button, icon state changes |
| md | 280ms | height/opacity reveals |
| lg | 420ms | section/card entrances |
| ease | `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)` | standard property transitions |
| ease | `cubic-bezier(0.33,0,0.15,1)` | transform-heavy moves |
| ease | `cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)` | symmetric in-out |

## Brief

Build a cream-paper enterprise pitch page for an AI/software product selling to large
buyers. Ground the whole page in a warm, slightly grey off-white (`#ECE8E3`) with near-
black ink (`#1B1814`); reserve colour for a single top announcement bar and black CTA
pills. Set every headline in an old-style serif at a size that reads like a pull-quote;
set every label, nav item, button and body line in a functional grotesque, never mixing
the two roles. Open on a serif headline over a thin-line diagram or a single muted photo,
with a work-email capture field beside the CTA. Below the fold, alternate: a dense logo
wall; a photo grid of use-case tiles labelled by vertical; paired stat cards with no
chart, just numbers and mono captions; a single embedded product video in a dark frame.
Close on a full-width dark or cream banner that restates the opening headline and repeats
the CTA.

## Image recipe

Documentary industrial photograph of [SUBJECT] — logistics yards, freight, ports, energy
infrastructure — shot in overcast or blue-hour light, desaturated toward cool grey-blue,
no people posed for camera, no gradient overlay, cropped tightly into a grid tile rather
than run full-bleed, contrast kept low so the photo reads as documentation, not a hero.

## Photo search

Unsplash first, Pexels second.
- "freight yard overcast blue hour"
- "wind turbines offshore muted"
- "warehouse logistics workers documentary"
- "shipping port cranes desaturated"

## Reference lock

Primary reference/direction: HappyRobot — cream enterprise pitch, serif claims over sans
proof, stat pairs as the persuasion device.
Preserve (3-5 traits): warm cream ground `#ECE8E3` with near-black ink `#1B1814`; old-style
serif (Tobias-class) reserved for headlines only; small functional-grotesque kickers and
body in one weight; proof delivered as logo walls and paired stat cards, never prose
claims; black pill CTAs as the only saturated shape on the page.
Borrow only (1-2): the single tan/accent announcement bar at the very top; the dark
embedded-video frame as a mid-page break.
Role rules: serif never sets a label or button; sans never sets a headline; colour
appears on at most two elements per screen (announcement bar, CTA); photography stays
desaturated within the page's tonal range, never full-saturation.
Media strategy: photo:unsplash — documentary industrial/logistics stills, muted and cool,
always cropped into a grid tile, never a full-bleed emotional hero.
Reject: full-bleed saturated hero photography; decorative line-art with no informational
role; more than one accent colour; centred marketing copy blocks; animated counters or
gradient CTAs.
Token commitments: bg `#ECE8E3`, bg-alt `#B7B2AA`, ink `#1B1814`, ink-soft `#584736`,
stone `#7F7D72`; display `Tobias` (or nearest old-style serif), body/label `Suisse Intl`
(or Suisse-class grotesque); headline set large with tight leading, body and labels one
consistent small size; grid strictly ruled, generous vertical whitespace between chapters.
